title.en: Volume 447 Biographies 234: Ding Baozhen, Li Hanzhang, Yang Changjun, Zhang Shusheng Younger Brother: Shu Ping, Wei Rongguang, Liu Bingzhang, Chen Shijie, Tao Mo, Li Xingrui, Shi Nianzu
title.raw: 卷447 列傳二百三十四 丁宝桢 李瀚章 杨昌濬 张树声弟：树屏 卫荣光 刘秉璋 陈士杰 陶模 李兴锐 史念祖

sentences.zh: 列傳二百三十四

translations.literal: Biographies, number two hundred thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 234

sentences.zh: 丁寶楨李瀚章楊昌濬張樹聲弟樹屏衛榮光

translations.literal: Ding Baozhen, Li Hanzhang, Yang Changjun, Zhang Shusheng, younger brother Shuping, Wei Rongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Baozhen, Li Hanzhang, Yang Changjun, Zhang Shusheng and his younger brother Shuping, and Wei Rongguang

sentences.zh: 劉秉璋陳士杰陶模李興銳史念祖

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhang, Chen Shijie, Tao Mo, Li Xingrui, Shi Nianzu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhang, Chen Shijie, Tao Mo, Li Xingrui, and Shi Nianzu

sentences.zh: 丁寶楨，字稚璜，貴州平遠人。

translations.literal: Ding Baozhen, courtesy name Zhihuang, was a native of Pingyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Baozhen, styled Zhihuang, came from Pingyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi and was chosen for the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 母喪里居，遵義楊隆喜反，斥家財募壯士八百捍鄉里，戰始不利，繼獲大勝。

translations.literal: While mourning his mother at home, Yang Longxi of Zunyi rebelled; he spent his family wealth to recruit eight hundred stalwart men to defend his native district; the fighting was at first unfavorable, then a great victory was won.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he remained in his home district. When Yang Longxi of Zunyi rose in rebellion, he poured out his family fortune to raise eight hundred fighting men to defend the countryside. The campaign began badly but ended in a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 服闋，會苗、教蜂起，巡撫蔣霨遠奏留軍，特旨授編修，增募至四千人，復平越、獨山諸城。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, the Miao and sectarian rebels swarmed up together; Governor Jiang Haoyuan memorialized to retain his army; by special edict he was appointed compiler; recruitment was increased to four thousand men; he recovered Pingyue, Dushan, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning ended, Miao and sectarian uprisings broke out across the region. Governor Jiang Haoyuan petitioned to keep his forces in the field, and an imperial order made him a compiler while he expanded his ranks to four thousand men and recaptured Pingyue, Dushan, and other towns.

sentences.zh: 十年，除知岳州府，始罷遣所募兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed prefect of Yuezhou and at last disbanded the troops he had recruited.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made prefect of Yuezhou and finally released the men he had raised.

sentences.zh: 虧餉巨萬，乃陳五百金案上，語眾曰：「與諸君共事久，今庫饋詘，徒手歸，奈何？」

translations.literal: Pay was short by tens of thousands; he then placed five hundred taels of gold on the table and said to the assembly: "I have worked with you all for a long time; now the treasury funds fall short—what are you to do returning empty-handed?"
translations.idiomatic: Pay was short by tens of thousands of taels. He laid five hundred taels of gold on the table and told the men, "We have served together a long time. The treasury cannot cover what is owed—how can you go home with nothing?"

sentences.zh: 眾泣曰：「公毀家紓難，我等敢他求乎？」

translations.literal: The men wept and said: "Your Lordship has ruined his household to relieve our distress—how dare we ask for anything else?"
translations.idiomatic: They wept and replied, "You have ruined your estate to save us—how could we ask for more?"

sentences.zh: 遂去。

translations.literal: Then they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Then they left.

sentences.zh: 越歲，調長沙。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was posted to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 有客軍數千，以無主將譁變，立請大府貸發三萬，斬五人，事遂定。

translations.literal: There were several thousand guest troops who mutinied for lack of a commanding general; he immediately requested thirty thousand taels on loan from the provincial administration, beheaded five men, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand auxiliary troops mutinied when they had no commander. He at once borrowed thirty thousand taels from the provincial treasury, executed five ringleaders, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 而其誅安得海事尤著人口。

translations.literal: But his execution of An Dehai was what people spoke of most widely.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was his execution of An Dehai that people remembered best.

sentences.zh: 安得海者，以奄人侍慈禧太后，頗用事。

translations.literal: An Dehai was a eunuch who attended Empress Dowager Cixi and wielded considerable power.
translations.idiomatic: An Dehai was a eunuch in attendance on Empress Dowager Cixi and had grown quite influential.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，乘樓船緣運河南下，旗繒殊異，稱有密遣。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year he traveled south along the Grand Canal on a tower boat, his banners and silk coverings conspicuously unusual, claiming he carried secret imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year he sailed south on the Grand Canal in a tower boat, flying unusual banners and silks and claiming a secret imperial mission.

sentences.zh: 所過招納權賄，無敢發者。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed he solicited bribes and favors, and none dared expose him.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he went he extorted favors and bribes, and no one dared report him.

sentences.zh: 至泰安，寶楨先已入告，使騎捕而守之。

translations.literal: When he reached Tai'an, Baozhen had already reported in advance and sent cavalry to arrest and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: At Tai'an, Baozhen had already alerted the authorities and sent cavalry to seize and hold him.

sentences.zh: 安得海猶大言，謂：「汝輩自速辜耳！」

translations.literal: An Dehai still spoke arrogantly, saying: "You are only hastening your own punishment!"
translations.idiomatic: An Dehai still blustered, "You are only bringing ruin on yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 傳送濟南，寶楨曰：「宦豎私出，非制。

translations.literal: He was sent under escort to Jinan. Baozhen said: "For a palace eunuch to go out on his own is against regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent under guard to Jinan. Baozhen argued, "A palace eunuch traveling on his own violates the rules.

sentences.zh: 且大臣未聞有命，必詐無疑。」

translations.literal: Moreover, no order has been heard from the high ministers—beyond doubt this is a fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, no high minister has announced any order—this is certainly a fraud."

sentences.zh: 奏上，遂正法。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and he was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up, and An Dehai was executed.

sentences.zh: 河決鄆城侯家林，運道梗，河臣議次年興工，寶楨謂宜及水涸時，力疾請自任。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst at Houjialin in Yancheng; the transport route was blocked; river officials proposed starting work the following year; Baozhen argued it should be done when the water subsided and, despite illness, vigorously requested to take charge himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke through at Houjialin in Yancheng and blocked the grain route, river officials wanted to wait until the next year. Baozhen insisted the work should begin while the water was low and, though ill, pressed to take personal charge.

sentences.zh: 水齧堤，植立不退，費半功倍。

translations.literal: The water gnawed at the dikes; he stood firm and would not withdraw, at double the cost for half the result.
translations.idiomatic: As the flood chewed at the dikes he stood his ground and would not retreat, spending twice the effort for half the gain.

sentences.zh: 又塞銅瓦廂決口，駐賈莊。

translations.literal: He also blocked the breach at Tongwaxiang and stationed himself at Jiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He also closed the breach at Tongwaxiang and made his headquarters at Jiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 聞日本構釁，遂密陳海防計，請築山東煙台、威海、登州砲台，設濼口製造機器局，從之。

translations.literal: Learning that Japan was provoking trouble, he confidentially submitted a coastal defense plan, requesting gun batteries at Yantai, Weihai, and Dengzhou in Shandong and a machine-manufacturing bureau at Luokou; the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Japan was stirring up trouble, he secretly proposed a coastal defense plan: fortify Yantai, Weihai, and Dengzhou in Shandong and establish a machine works at Luokou. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，代吳棠署四川總督。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Guangxu reign he replaced Wu Tang as acting governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he succeeded Wu Tang as acting governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 至即嚴劾貪墨吏，澄肅官方，建機器局，修都江堤，裁夫馬以恤民，革陋規以卹吏。

translations.literal: On arrival he sternly impeached corrupt officials, cleared and disciplined the bureaucracy, established a machine bureau, repaired the Dujiang embankment, reduced corvée labor and conveyance fees to relieve the people, and abolished corrupt practices to benefit officials.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he arrived he impeached corrupt officials, tightened discipline in the bureaucracy, founded a machine bureau, repaired the Dujiang dikes, cut corvée and transport levies to ease the people, and abolished abusive customs to protect officials.

sentences.zh: 又改鹽法，官運商銷，置總局瀘州，其井灶分置廠局，鹽岸分置岸局，歲增帑金百餘萬。

translations.literal: He also reformed the salt laws with government transport and merchant sales, set up a general bureau at Luzhou, established factory bureaus at various wells and pans and shore bureaus along the salt routes, increasing annual revenue by more than a million taels.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the salt trade as well: the government would transport and merchants would sell. He placed a central bureau at Luzhou, branch offices at the wells and pans, and shore offices along the routes, adding more than a million taels a year to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 而猾商姦吏不便所為，爭中以蜚語，於是臺諫交章糾奏。

translations.literal: But crafty merchants and corrupt officials were inconvenienced by his measures and vied to spread slanderous talk among them, whereupon censors submitted impeachments in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty merchants and corrupt officials, unhappy with his reforms, spread rumors against him, and censors soon filed one memorial of impeachment after another.

sentences.zh: 寶楨已坐堤毀鐫秩矣，而言者復劾停機器局，褫監工成綿龍茂道丁士彬、灌縣令陸葆德職，而尤龂龂爭鹽務。

translations.literal: Baozhen had already been demoted in rank for damage to the dikes, yet memorialists again impeached him for halting the machine bureau and stripped of office Cheng Mianlong, Mao Dao Ding Shibin, and Magistrate Lu Baode of Guan County—and they were especially contentious over the salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen had already been demoted for damage to the dikes, yet critics also attacked him for suspending the machine bureau and removed from office the supervisors Cheng Mianlong, Mao Dao Ding Shibin, and Magistrate Lu Baode of Guan County; the salt reforms drew the fiercest dispute of all.

sentences.zh: 上以川鹽有成效，勿為動。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the Sichuan salt measures had proven effective and ordered that they not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne judged the Sichuan salt reforms effective and told officials not to disturb them.

sentences.zh: 已而成都將軍恆訓覈覆堤工，亦摭及鹽運病商民、流弊大，寶楨抗辯。

translations.literal: Before long the Chengdu general Heng Xun reviewed the dike works and also seized on complaints that the salt transport harmed merchants and the people and that abuses were great; Baozhen argued in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward General Heng Xun of Chengdu inspected the dikes and repeated charges that the salt transport hurt merchants and the people and bred grave abuses. Baozhen answered each point.

sentences.zh: 上慮寶楨惑浮言，敕勿易初念。

translations.literal: The emperor feared Baozhen might be swayed by loose talk and ordered him not to alter his original resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried Baozhen might be swayed by gossip and ordered him to hold to his original plan.

sentences.zh: 尋予實授。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was given the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 寶楨彌自警勗，益興積穀，嚴督捕。

translations.literal: Baozhen redoubled his self-discipline, further promoted grain storage, and strictly supervised policing.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen tightened his own discipline all the more, expanded grain reserves, and enforced policing rigorously.

sentences.zh: 治蜀凡十年，初蒞事時，郭內月有盜劫，至是誅匪幾盡，聲為道不拾遺。

translations.literal: He governed Shu for ten years in all. When he first took office, there were monthly robberies within the city walls; by then bandits were nearly all exterminated, and it was said that things dropped on the road were not picked up.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Sichuan for ten years in all. When he arrived, robberies inside the city walls were a monthly occurrence; by the end bandits had been nearly wiped out, and people said no one would pick up what was dropped on the road.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒官，贈太子太保，諡文誠，予山東、四川、貴州建祠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died in office. He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wencheng. Temples were authorized in Shandong, Sichuan, and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died in office. He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the temple name Wencheng, and memorial temples were authorized in Shandong, Sichuan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 寶楨嚴剛有威。

translations.literal: Baozhen was stern, firm, and commanding.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen was stern and carried real authority.

sentences.zh: 其初至山東也，僧格林沁方蹙捻淄川，頗貴倨，見司道官不設坐。

translations.literal: When he first reached Shandong, Sengge Rinchen was pressing the Nian rebels at Zichuan and was quite proud and aloof; when he received circuit and prefectural officials he did not provide seats.
translations.idiomatic: When he first came to Shandong, Sengge Rinchen was tightening the siege on the Nian at Zichuan and carried himself with great pride; he received circuit and prefectural officials without offering them a seat.

sentences.zh: 寶楨投謁，告材官啟王，坐則見，否則罷，左右皆大驚。

translations.literal: Baozhen called on him and told the staff officer to announce to the prince: if there is a seat he will be received; otherwise he will leave. Those on either side were all greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen paid a visit and told the attendant to inform the prince: if he is offered a seat, Baozhen will enter; if not, he will withdraw. Everyone around them was astonished.

sentences.zh: 王服其強，為改容加禮。

translations.literal: The prince respected his firmness and changed his manner to show him greater courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The prince admired his nerve, changed his manner, and treated him with proper respect.

sentences.zh: 敬銘聞之，大稱異，至之日，親迓於郊。

translations.literal: When Jing Ming heard of this he greatly marveled; on the day Baozhen arrived he personally went out to the suburbs to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ming heard the story and was deeply impressed; when Baozhen arrived he went out to the suburbs himself to greet him.

sentences.zh: 自是事無大小，皆諮寶楨而後行。

translations.literal: From then on, matters great and small were all referred to Baozhen before action was taken.
translations.idiomatic: After that, nothing large or small was done until Baozhen had been consulted.

sentences.zh: 至今言吏治者，常與沈葆楨並稱，尤勵清操。

translations.literal: To this day, when people speak of good official governance, he is often named together with Shen Baozhen, and he was especially noted for encouraging integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even now, when officials are praised for good governance, his name is often linked with Shen Baozhen's, and he was especially admired for his clean conduct.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，僚屬集賻，始克成行雲。

translations.literal: When his coffin returned home, subordinates pooled condolence gifts before he could set out on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When his body was sent home, colleagues pooled funeral gifts before his family could afford the journey.

sentences.zh: 子五人，體常尤著名，官廣東布政使。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Tichang was especially well known and served as provincial treasurer of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons; Tichang was the most notable and rose to provincial treasurer of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 李瀚章，字筱泉，安徽合肥人，大學士鴻章兄也。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhang, courtesy name Xiaoquan, was a native of Hefei in Anhui and elder brother of Grand Secretary Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhang, styled Xiaoquan, came from Hefei in Anhui and was the elder brother of Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 瀚章以拔貢生為知縣，銓湖南，署永定，調益陽，改善化。

translations.literal: Hanzhang entered service as a county magistrate through the selected tribute-student route, was assigned to Hunan, acted at Yongding, was transferred to Yiyang, and then to Anhua.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang entered office as a county magistrate through the tribute-student route, was posted to Hunan, served at Yongding, then Yiyang, and finally Anhua.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓出治軍，檄主餉運，累至江西吉南贛寧道，調廣東督糧道，就遷按察使、布政使。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan took the field, he was ordered to take charge of supply transport; he rose in stages to the Jianan-Ganning circuit intendant in Jiangxi, was transferred to grain transport commissioner of Guangdong, and was then promoted to provincial judge and provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan raised an army, Hanzhang was ordered to manage supplies. He rose to circuit intendant for southern Jiangxi, became grain commissioner in Guangdong, and then provincial judge and treasurer.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，擢湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Tongzhi reign he was promoted to governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he was made governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時粵逆李世賢等聚福建，分犯贛南，窺兩楚，貴州苗匪、教匪又闌入楚界，而霆軍潰卒复竄湖、湘，三路告警。

translations.literal: At the time the Guangdong rebels Li Shixian and others gathered in Fujian, sent detachments to raid southern Jiangxi, and eyed the two Chu regions; Miao and sectarian bandits from Guizhou also crossed into Hunan; and routed soldiers of the Ting Army again fled into Hunan and Hunan—alarms on three fronts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Shixian and other Guangdong rebels massed in Fujian, raided southern Jiangxi, and threatened Hunan and Hubei; Miao and sectarian rebels from Guizhou crossed into Hunan as well; and routed soldiers from the Ting Army poured back into the two provinces—three fronts were in crisis at once.

sentences.zh: 瀚章至，則遣前江蘇按察使陳士杰壁郴州​​防閩賊，前雲南按察使趙煥聯壁岳州防叛卒，閩賊旋引去。

translations.literal: When Hanzhang arrived he sent the former Jiangsu provincial judge Chen Shijie to fortify Chenzhou against the Fujian rebels and the former Yunnan provincial judge Zhao Huanlian to fortify Yuezhou against the mutinous troops; the Fujian rebels soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Hanzhang sent the former Jiangsu judge Chen Shijie to hold Chenzhou against the Fujian rebels and the former Yunnan judge Zhao Huanlian to hold Yuezhou against the mutineers. The Fujian force soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 叛卒犯江西不得逞，則折入湘，犯攸縣，陷安仁、興寧、副將張義貴擊走之；

translations.literal: The mutinous troops, unable to succeed in Jiangxi, turned into Hunan, attacked You County, and seized Anren and Xingning; Vice Commander Zhang Yigui drove them off;
translations.idiomatic: Thwarted in Jiangxi, the mutineers swung into Hunan, struck You County, and took Anren and Xingning before Vice Commander Zhang Yigui drove them back;

sentences.zh: 士傑率軍會剿，遁入粵，卒就殲焉。

translations.literal: Shijie led troops in joint suppression; they fled into Guangdong and were finally annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie joined the pursuit, chased them into Guangdong, and they were finally destroyed.

sentences.zh: 先是瀚章遣總兵周洪印敗黔匪於邊界，又越境解銅仁圍，因奏言：「懸軍深入，兵家所忌，請敕新任貴州布政使兆琛緩赴任，專治軍事，與楚軍合。」

translations.literal: Earlier Hanzhang had sent Brigadier Zhou Hongyin to defeat Guizhou bandits on the border and also crossed the border to relieve the siege of Tongren; he therefore memorialized: "To drive a detached army deep into enemy country is what military strategists warn against; I request an order that the newly appointed Guizhou provincial treasurer Zhao Chen delay taking office and devote himself to military affairs, coordinating with the Hunan army."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hanzhang had sent Brigadier Zhou Hongyin to beat back Guizhou raiders on the border and crossed the border himself to lift the siege of Tongren. He then memorialized, "Driving a detached force deep into enemy territory is what strategists warn against. I ask that the newly appointed Guizhou treasurer Zhao Chen delay taking office and devote himself to military affairs, coordinating with the Hunan forces."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂遣已革知府李元度進剿思南、石阡教匪，兆琛、洪印進剿清江、台拱苗匪，所向克捷。

translations.literal: He then sent the dismissed prefect Li Yuandu to advance against the sectarian rebels in Sinan and Shiqian, while Zhao Chen and Hongyin advanced against the Miao bandits at Qingjiang and Taigong; wherever they went they won victories.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the dismissed prefect Li Yuandu against the sectarian rebels in Sinan and Shiqian, while Zhao Chen and Hongyin moved against the Miao at Qingjiang and Taigong. Every column met with success.

sentences.zh: 苗、教复蟻結，連竄晃州鳳凰廳，各軍躡擊，皆大破之，黔匪遂不敢窺楚境。

translations.literal: The Miao and sectarians again swarmed together and in succession fled into Huangzhou and Fenghuang subprefecture; the various armies pursued and all inflicted great defeats, so the Guizhou bandits no longer dared look toward the Hunan border.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao and sectarians rallied again and slipped into Huangzhou and Fenghuang. Pursuing columns broke them everywhere, and Guizhou raiders no longer dared threaten Hunan's frontier.

sentences.zh: 自盜起，國籓及胡林翼治師不主畫疆自守。

translations.literal: Since the rebellions arose, Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi in commanding armies did not advocate guarding fixed territorial boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: From the first uprisings, Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi had refused to treat provincial borders as limits when campaigning.

sentences.zh: 瀚章久習楚軍，既受任，即出境討賊，亦其風類也。

translations.literal: Hanzhang had long been accustomed to the Hunan army ways; once he received his appointment he at once crossed the border to suppress bandits—this too was of that same tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang had long served in the Hunan army tradition; once appointed he too crossed provincial lines to fight rebels, in the same spirit.

sentences.zh: 六年，調撫江蘇。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to be governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Jiangsu as governor.

sentences.zh: 未至，署湖廣總督。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was appointed acting governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the Jiangsu post he was made acting governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 七年，調浙江，再署湖廣總督，旋實授。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Zhejiang, again acted as governor-general of Huguang, and shortly received the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was posted to Zhejiang, served again as acting governor-general of Huguang, and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，調四川。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was transferred to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he was transferred to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，還督湖廣。

translations.literal: The following year he returned to govern Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to govern Huguang.

sentences.zh: 瀚章性簡靜，更事久，習知民情偽，務與休息。

translations.literal: Hanzhang's nature was simple and quiet; he had long experience in office and was well acquainted with the truth and falsehood of popular sentiment, and he strove to give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang was plain and unassuming by nature. Long experience had taught him how people really lived, and he aimed above all to let the region recover.

sentences.zh: 其督湖廣最久，前後四至，皆與弟鴻章更迭受代，其母累年不移武昌官所，人以為榮。

translations.literal: He governed Huguang longest of all, coming there four times in all, each time alternating in office with his younger brother Hongzhang; his mother for many years did not move from the official residence at Wuchang, and people regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Huguang longer than anywhere else, serving there four times in all, each stint alternating with his brother Hongzhang. Their mother kept the family residence at Wuchang for years without moving, which people took as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 尋遭憂去官，家居六年，再起授漕運總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he left office on account of mourning, remained at home for six years, and was then recalled and appointed grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to mourn a parent and stayed home six years before being recalled as grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移督兩廣。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to govern the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 粵俗舊有闈姓捐，四成助餉，巡撫馬丕瑤議革之。

translations.literal: Guangdong custom had long had the examination-hall surname levy, forty percent of which went to aid military pay; Governor Ma Peiyao proposed abolishing it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had long levied a surname tax tied to the civil examinations, with forty percent earmarked for military funds. Governor Ma Peiyao proposed abolishing it.

sentences.zh: 會日本構釁，瀚章請循舊收繳備海防，時論大譁，遂以疾歸。

translations.literal: When Japan provoked hostilities, Hanzhang requested continuing to collect the old levy for coastal defense; public opinion was greatly outraged, and he retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan began provoking trouble, Hanzhang asked to keep collecting the old levy for coastal defense. Public outrage was fierce, and he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 又數年，卒，諡勤恪。

translations.literal: Several years later he died and was given the posthumous title Qinke.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he died and was given the posthumous title Qinke.

sentences.zh: 子十人，經畬，翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: He had ten sons; Jingshe served as Hanlin lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons; Jingshe became a Hanlin lecturer.

sentences.zh: 楊昌濬，字石泉，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Yang Changjun, courtesy name Shiquan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Changjun, styled Shiquan, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 粵寇亂，以諸生從羅澤南治團練，出援湖北，連复廣濟、黃梅，敘訓導。

translations.literal: When the Guangdong rebels rose, as a licentiate he followed Luo Zinan in organizing local militia, went out to aid Hubei, and in succession recovered Guangji and Huangmei; he was rewarded with the rank of director of studies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping rebellion spread, he joined Luo Zinan as a student to organize local militia, marched into Hubei, and recaptured Guangji and Huangmei in succession, earning appointment as director of studies.

sentences.zh: 從征贛、皖，戰楓樹嶺，下德興，戰高沙，下婺源，頻有功，遷知縣。

translations.literal: He campaigned in Jiangxi and Anhui, fought at Fengshuling, took Dexing, fought at Gaosha, took Wuyuan, won repeated merit, and was promoted to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Jiangxi and Anhui, fought at Fengshuling and took Dexing, fought at Gaosha and took Wuyuan, won repeated distinction, and was promoted to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從左宗棠入浙，規江山，與劉典、劉璈分三路攻石門，破寇卡數重。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Zuo Zongtang into Zhejiang to invest Jiangshan; with Liu Dian and Liu Ao he divided into three routes to attack Shimen and broke several rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Zuo Zongtang into Zhejiang to besiege Jiangshan. With Liu Dian and Liu Ao he split into three columns against Shimen and stormed several rebel stockades.

sentences.zh: 進取花園港，縱火燔其棚，會天雨，止。

translations.literal: Advancing to take Huayuangang, he set fire and burned their sheds; rain came and the operation halted.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Huayuangang, he set fire to the rebel shelters, but rain fell and the attack had to stop.

sentences.zh: 其秋，規龍遊，昌濬禦寇蓮塘，破之；

translations.literal: That autumn, investing Longyou, Changjun met the rebels at Liantang and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, while investing Longyou, Changjun met the rebels at Liantang and routed them;

sentences.zh: 又敗之孟塘，寇逸。

translations.literal: he defeated them again at Mengtang and the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: he beat them again at Mengtang, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 李世賢聞警，遣悍黨赴救，中路寇方攻劉培元營，昌濬自山下擊，寇大潰，遷知衢州府。

translations.literal: Li Shixian, hearing the alarm, sent fierce fighters to the rescue; rebels in the center were just attacking Liu Peiyuan's camp when Changjun struck from below the hill; the rebels were utterly routed and he was promoted to prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shixian sent elite troops to relieve the city. While rebels in the center were assaulting Liu Peiyuan's camp, Changjun attacked downhill and broke them completely. He was then made prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，師偪龍遊城南，築三壘。

translations.literal: The following year the army pressed the south of Longyou city and built three forts.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the army pressed the south wall of Longyou and built three fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 寇夜奔，昌濬躡之湯溪。

translations.literal: The rebels fled by night; Changjun pursued them to Tangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled by night, and Changjun pursued them to Tangxi.

sentences.zh: 城拔，授糧儲道。

translations.literal: When the city was taken he was appointed grain storage commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell he was made grain storage commissioner.

sentences.zh: 與蔣益澧合兵萬三千戰餘杭城西北，寇益浚壕樹壘拒師。

translations.literal: Joining Jiang Yili with thirteen thousand troops he fought northwest of Yuhang city; the rebels further deepened the moats and built stockades to resist the army.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiang Yili he united thirteen thousand men and fought northwest of Yuhang. The rebels deepened the moats and threw up stockades to hold the army back.

sentences.zh: 昌濬攻北門，寇出戰，會諸軍擊之，寇卻，昌濬連夷五卡。

translations.literal: Changjun attacked the north gate; the rebels came out to fight; the various armies joined the attack and the rebels fell back; Changjun in succession destroyed five stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Changjun assaulted the north gate. When the rebels sallied out, allied columns joined the fight and drove them back. Changjun then took five stockades in a row.

sentences.zh: 次日，攻林清塘，去城北十里，汪海洋老巢也，昌濬覘寇壘阻水，慮日暮為寇乘，乃退師。

translations.literal: The next day he attacked Linqingtang, ten li north of the city, Wang Haiyang's old stronghold; Changjun observed that the rebel stockades were blocked by water and feared that at dusk the rebels would take advantage, so he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he attacked Linqingtang, ten li north of the city and Wang Haiyang's old headquarters. Seeing the rebel camps cut off by water and fearing a night counterattack, he pulled his troops back.

sentences.zh: 又明年，規武康，復其城。

translations.literal: The year after that he invested Wukang and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he besieged Wukang and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 進略湖州，寇竄泗安、梅溪，昌濬自簰頭進桐嶺扼之，北攻安吉，追寇至孝豐，遇湖州敗寇，復與璈合攻之，降者七千餘人，輒解散。

translations.literal: Advancing against Huzhou, the rebels fled to Si'an and Meixi; Changjun advanced from Paitou to Tongling to block them, attacked north toward Anji, pursued the rebels to Xiaofeng, met defeated rebels from Huzhou, again joined Ao in attacking them; more than seven thousand surrendered and were at once disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing toward Huzhou, he found rebels slipping toward Si'an and Meixi. Changjun moved from Paitou to hold Tongling, struck north toward Anji, and pursued the enemy to Xiaofeng. There he met routed rebels from Huzhou, joined Liu Ao in a combined attack, and accepted the surrender of more than seven thousand men, whom he immediately disbanded.

sentences.zh: 浙西平，遷鹽運使，累擢布政使。

translations.literal: When western Zhejiang was pacified he was transferred to salt transport commissioner and was promoted in stages to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: When western Zhejiang was pacified he became salt commissioner and rose step by step to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 九年，除巡撫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made governor.

sentences.zh: 巡視鎮海海口，條具見聞，陳大恉，謂宜師敵伎，練勁旅，修築砲台，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: He inspected the Zhenhai sea mouth, set forth his observations in detail, and stated his great purpose, saying the court should learn the enemy's techniques, train crack troops, and build gun batteries; the emperor praised and accepted his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the harbor at Zhenhai and submitted a detailed report urging the court to study enemy methods, train elite troops, and build coastal batteries. The emperor approved his recommendations warmly.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷方銳意求治，詔舉賢才，昌濬以糧道如山四人應，力荐甘肅知縣陶模才器遠大，卒如所言。

translations.literal: At that time the court was keenly seeking good governance and issued an edict to recommend talented men; Changjun nominated four men including the grain commissioner Rushan, strongly recommending Tao Mo, magistrate of Gansu, for far-reaching talent and capacity; in the end it proved as he said.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then eager for reform and called for recommendations of talent. Changjun nominated four officials, including grain commissioner Rushan, and strongly recommended Tao Mo, magistrate in Gansu, for exceptional ability. Events later proved him right.

sentences.zh: 坐餘杭葛畢氏案褫職。

translations.literal: He was stripped of office on account of the Ge and Bi clans case in Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his post over the Ge and Bi clans case in Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，起佐新疆軍事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was recalled to assist in military affairs in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was recalled to assist military operations in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 數遷至漕運總督。

translations.literal: After several promotions he reached the post of grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年，法人擾海疆，朝旨以閩事亟，命宗棠為欽差大臣，主軍務，昌濬與穆圖善佐之，張佩綸則會辦也。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the French disturbed the coastal frontier; the court, judging Fujian affairs urgent, appointed Zongtang imperial commissioner to direct military affairs, with Changjun and Mutushan as his assistants and Zhang Peilun as joint coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the French threatened the coast. With Fujian in crisis, the court made Zuo Zongtang imperial commissioner in charge of military affairs, with Changjun and Mutushan as his deputies and Zhang Peilun as joint coordinator.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督何璟自以不諳兵事，請解職，遂命昌濬代之。

translations.literal: Governor-General He Jing of Fujian and Zhejiang, considering himself unversed in military affairs, requested to be relieved of office, and Changjun was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Jing of Fujian and Zhejiang, admitting he knew little of military affairs, asked to step down, and Changjun was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 昌濬未至軍，而佩綸已遁，事下宗棠、昌濬。

translations.literal: Changjun had not yet reached the army when Peilun had already fled; the matter was referred down to Zongtang and Changjun.
translations.idiomatic: Changjun had not yet reached the front when Zhang Peilun had already fled. The case was referred to Zuo Zongtang and Changjun for investigation.

sentences.zh: 覆奏入，上責其袒護，移督陝甘，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When the follow-up memorial arrived, the emperor rebuked him for partiality, transferred him to govern Shaanxi and Gansu, and added the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his reply reached the throne, the emperor blamed him for favoritism, moved him to the Shaanxi-Gansu post, and made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 昌濬性和巽，而務為姑息。

translations.literal: Changjun's nature was mild and compliant, and he strove to be indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: Changjun was mild by nature and inclined toward leniency.

sentences.zh: 督甘日，左右通回匪，莫能製，槍械反資寇，遂釀成湟中河、狄亂。

translations.literal: While governing Gansu, those around him colluded with Muslim rebels and could not be controlled; firearms instead supplied the bandits, and thus the disorders of Huangzhong, He, and Di were brought about.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Gansu his staff colluded with Muslim rebels beyond his control. Arms meant for the government instead reached the bandits, helping spark the uprisings in Huangzhong, He, and Di.

sentences.zh: 昌濬檄各路募土勇助戰守，電令提督雷正綰往河州鎮懾，張永清往西寧策應，蘇員嶼往巴燕戎甘、都堂駐防，並具起事顛末以上。

translations.literal: Changjun ordered the various routes to recruit local braves to aid in defense, telegraphed Brigadier Lei Zhengwan to go to Hezhou to overawe the rebels, Zhang Yongqing to move toward Xining in support, Su Yuanyu toward Bayan and the Gansu frontier with the governor-general stationed on defense, and set forth the full course of how the trouble arose in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Changjun called on every district to raise local militia, wired Brigadier Lei Zhengwan to Hezhou to overawe the rebels, Zhang Yongqing toward Xining in support, and Su Yuanyu toward Bayan while he himself held the capital region. He also sent up a full account of how the revolt began.

sentences.zh: 事聞，嚴旨責其庸瞶，乃罷官。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, a stern edict rebuked his incompetence and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an imperial reprimand condemned his incompetence and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，卒，釋處分。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died and his penalties were lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-third year, and the penalties against him were set aside.

sentences.zh: 嗣以魏光燾請，予甘肅建祠。

translations.literal: Later, at Wei Guangtao's request, a memorial temple was authorized in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Wei Guangtao's request, a memorial temple was authorized in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 張樹聲，字振軒，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shusheng, courtesy name Zhenxuan, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shusheng, styled Zhenxuan, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 粵寇擾皖北，以禀生與其弟樹珊、樹屏治團殺賊。

translations.literal: When Guangdong rebels troubled northern Anhui, as a petitioning student he and his younger brothers Shushan and Shuping organized local militia to kill bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels from the south ravaged northern Anhui, he and his brothers Shushan and Shuping, though only students submitting petitions, organized local militia to fight them.

sentences.zh: 复越境出擊，連下含山、六安、英山、霍山、潛山、無為；

translations.literal: He again crossed the border to strike out, and in succession took Hanshan, Lu'an, Yingshan, Huoshan, Qianshan, and Wuwei;
translations.idiomatic: He crossed provincial lines to attack and in succession took Hanshan, Lu'an, Yingshan, Huoshan, Qianshan, and Wuwei;

sentences.zh: 而太湖一役，以五百人陷陣，擊退陳玉成眾數万，功尤盛，复力行堅壁清野法。

translations.literal: At the battle of Taihu, with five hundred men he plunged into the line of battle and drove back Chen Yucheng's force of tens of thousands—his merit was especially great—and he again vigorously practiced the fortified-village and scorched-earth method.
translations.idiomatic: At Taihu he led five hundred men into the thick of battle and repulsed Chen Yucheng's army of tens of thousands, his greatest feat of all. He also enforced the fortified-village and scorched-earth policy with vigor.

sentences.zh: 其時劉銘傳、周盛波、潘鼎新輩皆相繼築堡，聯爲一氣，皖北破碎，獨合肥西鄉差全。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Mingchuan, Zhou Shengbo, Pan Dingxin, and others all built fortified villages in succession, linking into one network; northern Anhui was shattered, but the western townships of Hefei alone remained comparatively intact.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mingchuan, Zhou Shengbo, Pan Dingxin, and others built fortified villages in turn until their lines formed a single network. Northern Anhui lay in ruins, but the western townships around Hefei alone stayed largely intact.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓檄守蕪湖，調無為，遷知府。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan ordered him to guard Wuhu, transferred him to Wuwei, and promoted him to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan ordered him to hold Wuhu, then Wuwei, and promoted him to prefect.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從李鴻章援上海。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Li Hongzhang to relieve Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Li Hongzhang to relieve Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 鴻章立淮軍，與銘傳等分領其眾，從克江陰，晉道員。

translations.literal: Hongzhang established the Huai Army and divided command of its forces with Mingchuan and others; Shusheng followed in the capture of Jiangyin and was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang formed the Huai Army and shared command with Mingchuan and others. Shusheng helped take Jiangyin and was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 鴻章親視婁門程學啟軍，遣樹聲援蕩口，破謝家橋，逐北至齊門，又敗之黃埭，學啟遂偪城而軍，於是婁門寇道始絕。

translations.literal: Hongzhang personally inspected Cheng Xueqi's army at Loumen and sent Shusheng to aid Dangkou; he broke Xiejiaqiao, pursued north to Qimen, and defeated the enemy again at Huangdai; Xueqi then pressed the city with his army, and from then on the rebel route at Loumen was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang inspected Cheng Xueqi's army at Loumen and sent Shusheng to support Dangkou. Shusheng broke Xiejiaqiao, drove the enemy north to Qimen, and beat them again at Huangdai. Xueqi then pressed the city, and the rebel route through Loumen was finally severed.

sentences.zh: 二年，攻無錫、金匱，擊寇芙蓉山，大破之，奪獲戰艦器械不可稱計，賜號卓勇巴圖魯，予三品服。

translations.literal: In the second year he attacked Wuxi and Jingui, struck the rebels at Furongshan and inflicted a great defeat, capturing warships and weapons beyond counting; he was granted the title Zhuoyong Batulu and given third-rank dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he attacked Wuxi and Jingui, routed the rebels at Furongshan, and seized warships and arms beyond count. He received the title Zhuoyong Batulu and third-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 樹聲乘勝趨常州。

translations.literal: Shusheng pressed the victory toward Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng pressed on toward Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，攻河乾二十餘營，盡破之。

translations.literal: After a year he attacked more than twenty camps along the riverbank and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he stormed more than twenty camps along the river and destroyed them all.

sentences.zh: 城拔，進复浙江湖州，詔以按察使記名。

translations.literal: When the city fell he advanced to recover Huzhou in Zhejiang and was recorded by edict for appointment as provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell he recovered Huzhou in Zhejiang and was marked for appointment as provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 四年，署江蘇徐海道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he acted as Xuhai circuit intendant of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he served as acting Xuhai circuit intendant in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 尋授直隸按察使，赴大名督防務。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed provincial judge of Zhili and went to Daming to supervise defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made provincial judge of Zhili and went to Daming to supervise frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 九年，調補山西。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to fill a post in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 越二年，擢漕運總督，署江蘇巡撫，十三年，實授。

translations.literal: Two years later he was promoted to grain transport commissioner and acted as governor of Jiangsu; in the thirteenth year he received the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became grain transport commissioner and acting governor of Jiangsu, receiving the full Jiangsu appointment in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 遭繼母憂，歸。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his stepmother and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his stepmother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，起授貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was recalled and appointed governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu he was recalled as governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 適廣東總兵李揚才據靈山，構匪擾越南，朝旨調樹聲撫廣西治之。

translations.literal: Just then Guangdong Brigadier Li Yangcai held Lingshan and stirred up bandits to trouble Vietnam; the court ordered Shusheng transferred to govern Guangxi to deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Brigadier Li Yangcai of Guangdong held Lingshan and used bandits to stir trouble in Vietnam. The court transferred Shusheng to Guangxi to handle the crisis.

sentences.zh: 事寧，擢總督，先後剿平西林苗匪、武宣積匪。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was promoted to governor-general and in succession suppressed Miao bandits in Xilin and long-standing bandits in Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored he became governor-general and in turn pacified Miao rebels in Xilin and entrenched bandits in Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 八年，鴻章喪母歸葬，樹聲攝直督任。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Hongzhang returned home to bury his mother; Shusheng acted in the Zhili governor-general's post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Hongzhang went home to bury his mother, and Shusheng served as acting governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 值朝鮮亂作，日使花房義質將兵五百入王京，迫朝議約，樹聲飛檄吳長慶等赴之，遂成約，尋盟而還。

translations.literal: When disorder broke out in Korea, the Japanese minister Hanabusa Yoshimichi led five hundred troops into the royal capital and forced Korea to negotiate a treaty; Shusheng urgently dispatched Wu Changqing and others thither, a treaty was concluded, and they soon withdrew after making alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Korea fell into turmoil, Japanese minister Hanabusa Yoshimichi marched five hundred troops into the capital and forced a treaty on the court. Shusheng urgently sent Wu Changqing and others, a treaty was signed, and the forces withdrew after exchanging pledges.

sentences.zh: 於是長慶等宵攻亂黨，悉殲其渠，亂乃定，樹聲奏令長慶暫戍朝，上嘉其能，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Thereupon Changqing and others attacked the rebels by night, annihilated their leaders entirely, and the disorder was settled; Shusheng memorialized that Changqing should temporarily garrison Korea; the emperor praised his ability and added the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing then attacked the rebels by night and killed their leaders, ending the crisis. Shusheng asked that Changqing remain in Korea for a time. The emperor praised his handling of the affair and made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，還督兩廣。

translations.literal: The following year he returned to govern the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to govern Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 會法越構兵，即以法人侵逼狀上聞。

translations.literal: When France and Vietnam came into conflict, he at once reported the French invasion and pressure to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When France and Vietnam went to war, he immediately reported the French advance to the court.

sentences.zh: 逮北寧陷，自請解總督職專治軍，報可。

translations.literal: When Bac Ninh fell he requested to be relieved of the governor-generalship to devote himself solely to military affairs; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After Bac Ninh fell he asked to give up the governorship and command the army full time. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 复坐按事不實，革職留任。

translations.literal: He was again punished for handling a case untruthfully, stripped of rank but retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later punished for mishandling an investigation, demoted in rank but kept in post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，病卒，諡靖達，予直隸、江蘇及本籍建祠。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness and was given the posthumous title Jingda; memorial temples were authorized in Zhili, Jiangsu, and his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness and received the posthumous title Jingda. Memorial temples were authorized in Zhili, Jiangsu, and his home district.

sentences.zh: 樹珊自有傳。

translations.literal: Shushan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shushan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 樹屏，以收復江蘇各州縣，積勳至副將。

translations.literal: Shuping, through recovering the various prefectures and counties of Jiangsu, accumulated merit until he reached the rank of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shuping rose to vice commander on merit earned recovering Jiangsu's prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 從征捻，駐周家口，戰數捷。

translations.literal: Campaigning against the Nian, he was stationed at Zhoujiakou and won several victories.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against the Nian, he was posted at Zhoujiakou and won several battles.

sentences.zh: 捻平，擢提督，賜號額騰額巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the Nian were pacified he was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief and granted the title Etengge Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nian were suppressed he became provincial commander-in-chief and received the title Etengge Batulu.

sentences.zh: 赴晉防河。

translations.literal: He went to Shanxi to defend the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Shanxi to defend the Yellow River frontier.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，徙守河曲、保德。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he was transferred to guard Hequ and Baode.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he was posted to Hequ and Baode.

sentences.zh: 會皖軍赴援烏魯木齊，甘肅流賊曹洪照竄後山，樹屏適奉檄詣省，聞警，乘大雪追擊之。

translations.literal: When the Anhui army went to aid Urumqi, the Gansu bandit Cao Hongzhao fled into the rear hills; Shuping happened to be ordered to the provincial capital, heard the alarm, and pursued in heavy snow.
translations.idiomatic: When Anhui troops marched to relieve Urumqi, the Gansu bandit Cao Hongzhao slipped into the hills behind the lines. Shuping was on his way to the capital when he heard the alarm and pursued through heavy snow.

sentences.zh: 事定，賜頭品服，授太原鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was granted first-rank dress and appointed commander of Taiyuan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he received first-rank dress and command of the Taiyuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 移防包頭，調大同。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defend Baotou and then to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Baotou, then transferred to Datong.

sentences.zh: 十三年，乞休。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 既歿，鴻章狀其績以上，予優恤，太原建祠。

translations.literal: After his death Hongzhang set forth his achievements in a memorial; generous condolence grants were given and a temple was built at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Hongzhang memorialized his achievements. The court granted generous posthumous honors and authorized a temple at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 衛榮光，字靜瀾，河南新鄉人。

translations.literal: Wei Rongguang, courtesy name Jinglan, was a native of Xinxiang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rongguang, styled Jinglan, came from Xinxiang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the second year of Xianfeng, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 九年，湖北巡撫胡林翼奏調赴軍，隨荊州將軍多隆阿攻剿黃州各郡，轉戰入安徽，平賊壘百餘，克太湖、潛山。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Hunan Governor Hu Linyi memorialized to transfer him to the army; he followed Jingzhou General Dolonga in attacking and suppressing the various prefectures of Huangzhou, fought his way into Anhui, leveled more than a hundred rebel stockades, and took Taihu and Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Governor Hu Linyi of Hubei had him transferred to the field. With General Dolonga of Jingzhou he campaigned through Huangzhou into Anhui, destroyed more than a hundred rebel strongpoints, and took Taihu and Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 捷入，以侍講待簡。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was held for appointment as expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported he was marked for appointment as Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 林翼督師勦賊，榮光從，常以少擊眾。

translations.literal: Linyi directed the army in suppressing bandits and Rongguang followed, often striking the many with the few.
translations.idiomatic: When Linyi commanded the suppression campaigns, Rongguang followed him and often beat larger forces with smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 林翼卒，乃還京供職。

translations.literal: When Linyi died he returned to the capital to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: After Linyi died he returned to the capital to resume court duties.

sentences.zh: 道經新鄉，適山東竄匪入境，遂與知縣丁士選集團捍衛。

translations.literal: Passing through Xinxiang on the way, bandits fleeing from Shandong had just entered the district; he therefore joined with Magistrate Ding Shixuan in organizing militia for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through his home district of Xinxiang, he found bandits fleeing from Shandong crossing the border. He joined Magistrate Ding Shixuan in raising militia to defend the area.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，入都，補翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he entered the capital and was appointed Hanlin lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he reached the capital and was appointed Hanlin lecturer.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢侍講學士，疏陳剿匪、防河事宜。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Hanlin academician and submitted a memorial setting forth plans for suppressing bandits and defending the river.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Hanlin academician and memorialized on bandit suppression and river defense.

sentences.zh: 是年授濟東泰武臨道，署山東鹽運使、按察使。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Jidong-Taiwu-Lin circuit intendant and acted as Shandong salt commissioner and provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became circuit intendant for eastern Shandong and acted as salt commissioner and provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 四年，捻首賴文光、張總愚竄山東，巡撫閻敬銘奏委榮光督辦河防。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Nian leaders Lai Wenguang and Zhang Zongyu fled into Shandong; Governor Yan Jingming memorialized to entrust Rongguang with supervising river defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Nian leaders Lai Wenguang and Zhang Zongyu slipped into Shandong. Governor Yan Jingming put Rongguang in charge of river defense.

sentences.zh: 榮光以賊無現糧，利速戰，堅諭各軍嚴守困賊。

translations.literal: Rongguang held that the bandits had no ready grain and favored swift battle, and he sternly ordered the various armies to hold fast and wear the bandits down.
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang reasoned that the rebels had little grain on hand and would want a quick fight, and he ordered every unit to hold firm and starve them out.

sentences.zh: 賊乘夜偷渡，榮光燃砲擊之，諸軍繼進，賊大敗。

translations.literal: The bandits crossed by night in a stealth crossing; Rongguang fired cannon at them, the various armies followed up, and the bandits were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels tried a night crossing, Rongguang opened fire with artillery. Allied columns joined the attack and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 六年，卸運使任，仍兼署按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he relinquished the salt commissioner's post but still concurrently acted as provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he left the salt post but continued to act as provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 時賊勢復振，巡撫丁寶楨督師出境，省城兵單餉竭。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits' strength revived; Governor Ding Baozhen led the army out of the province, and in the provincial capital troops were few and funds exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rallied again while Governor Ding Baozhen led the army beyond the province, leaving the capital thinly garrisoned and nearly out of funds.

sentences.zh: 榮光募民團助守，賊屢逼城下，卒不能犯。

translations.literal: Rongguang recruited local militia to aid in defense; the bandits repeatedly pressed the city walls but in the end could not break in.
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang raised local militia to help defend the city. The rebels pressed the walls several times but never broke through.

sentences.zh: 旋以父憂歸。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he returned home on account of mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 十二年，起江安糧道，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was recalled as Jiang'an grain commissioner and acted as provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was recalled as Jiang'an grain commissioner and acting provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，授安徽按察使，遷浙江布政使，護理巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was appointed provincial judge of Anhui, transferred to provincial treasurer of Zhejiang, and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he became provincial judge of Anhui, then treasurer of Zhejiang, acting as governor.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was appointed governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his mother, and after the mourning period became governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 八年，調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 台灣道劉璈被重劾，詔刑部尚書錫珍往按，復命榮光赴台會鞫。

translations.literal: Taiwan Circuit Intendant Liu Ao was heavily impeached; the emperor ordered Minister of Justice Xi Zhen to go investigate and further ordered Rongguang to go to Taiwan to join in the trial.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwan intendant Liu Ao faced serious impeachment, the court sent Minister of Justice Xi Zhen to investigate and ordered Rongguang to join the inquiry in Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 榮光言：「璈總營務，開支浮冒，罪當死；

translations.literal: Rongguang said: "Ao oversaw camp affairs and his expenditures were inflated and fraudulent—the crime warrants death;
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang argued, "Liu Ao oversaw military affairs and his accounts were grossly inflated—a capital offense;

sentences.zh: 然其治事疏節闊目，政頗便民，故台地番民至今有屍祝者。

translations.literal: yet in governing he was broad in scope and easygoing in manner, and his policies greatly benefited the people, so among the aborigines of Taiwan to this day some offer sacrifice before his image.
translations.idiomatic: yet he governed with a broad hand and policies that genuinely helped the people. Even now some indigenous people in Taiwan still offer sacrifice in his name.

sentences.zh: 請從寬典。」

translations.literal: I request leniency under the law."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the court show mercy.

sentences.zh: 其持法嚴而能恕皆此類。

translations.literal: His upholding the law with severity yet ability to forgive were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His severity in law paired with willingness to forgive was typical of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調浙江巡撫，再調山西。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to governor of Zhejiang, then again to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made governor of Zhejiang, then transferred again to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞休。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 劉秉璋，字仲良，安徽廬江人。

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhang, courtesy name Zhongliang, was a native of Lujiang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhang, styled Zhongliang, came from Lujiang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 參欽差張芾軍，敘知縣。

translations.literal: He joined Imperial Commissioner Zhang Fu's army and was rewarded with appointment as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Imperial Commissioner Zhang Fu's army and was rewarded with appointment as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章治兵上海，調赴營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang was raising troops at Shanghai and transferred him to camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Li Hongzhang was raising troops at Shanghai, he was transferred to the front.

sentences.zh: 洋將戈登所練常勝軍故駐滬，滋驕。

translations.literal: The Ever-Victorious Army trained by the foreign general Gordon had long been stationed at Shanghai and had grown arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Gordon's Ever-Victorious Army had long been stationed in Shanghai and had grown arrogant.

sentences.zh: 淮軍初至，服陋械絀，西弁或侮笑之。

translations.literal: When the Huai Army first arrived, their dress was shabby and their weapons poor, and Western officers sometimes mocked them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai Army first arrived, their uniforms were shabby and their arms poor, and some Western officers laughed at them.

sentences.zh: 秉璋語眾曰：「此不足病也，顧吾曹能戰否耳。」

translations.literal: Bingzhang said to the men: "This is nothing to worry about; what matters is whether we can fight."
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang told his men, "That is nothing to worry about. What matters is whether we can fight."

sentences.zh: 明年，從克常熟、太倉。

translations.literal: The following year he followed in the capture of Changshu and Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he helped take Changshu and Taicang.

sentences.zh: 鴻章使別募一軍圖嘉善分寇勢，遂提兵五千赴難，克楓涇、西塘，遷侍講。

translations.literal: Hongzhang had him separately recruit an army to target Jiashan and divide the rebels' strength; he then led five thousand troops to the crisis, took Fengjing and Xitang, and was promoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang had him raise a separate force to threaten Jiashan and split the rebel front. He led five thousand men into action, took Fengjing and Xitang, and was promoted to Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 進攻張涇匯，約水師夾擊，彈丸貫胯下，不少卻，卒克之。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Zhangjinghui, he arranged a pincer with the naval force; a bullet passed through below his crotch but he did not retreat in the least, and in the end took it.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Zhangjinghui, he coordinated with the navy in a pincer. A bullet passed through his groin, but he did not retreat and finally took the position.

sentences.zh: 規平湖，其酋陳殿選降，於是乍浦、海鹽、澉浦皆反正。

translations.literal: Investing Pinghu, its chieftain Chen Dianxuan surrendered, and thereupon Zha Pu, Haiyan, and Ganpu all returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Pinghu, he accepted the surrender of rebel leader Chen Dianxuan, and Zha Pu, Haiyan, and Ganpu all returned to the government side.

sentences.zh: 又明年，與程學啟攻嘉興，秉璋入東門燔藥庫，寇駴亂，眾軍乘之，城拔。

translations.literal: The year after that, with Cheng Xueqi he attacked Jiaxing; Bingzhang entered the east gate and burned the powder magazine; the rebels were terrified and thrown into disorder; the armies pressed the advantage and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he and Cheng Xueqi attacked Jiaxing. Bingzhang entered the east gate and set fire to the powder magazine. The rebels panicked, the allied columns pressed in, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 進取湖州，攻吳漊、南潯，所向摧靡。

translations.literal: Advancing to take Huzhou, he attacked Wulian and Nanxun; wherever he went he swept all before him.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing toward Huzhou, he attacked Wulian and Nanxun and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 浙西平，賜號振勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When western Zhejiang was pacified he was granted the title Zhenyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When western Zhejiang was pacified he received the title Zhenyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 歷遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 四年，授江蘇按察使，從曾國籓討捻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed provincial judge of Jiangsu and followed Zeng Guofan in suppressing the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became provincial judge of Jiangsu and joined Zeng Guofan against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 時捻騎飆疾，國籓與鴻章皆主圈制策，秉璋力讚之，破捻豐、沛、宿遷南，追至倉家集，捻大潰。

translations.literal: At that time the Nian cavalry were swift as a whirlwind; Guofan and Hongzhang both advocated the encirclement strategy; Bingzhang strongly endorsed it, defeated the Nian south of Feng, Pei, and Suqian, pursued to Cangjiaji, and the Nian were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian cavalry were lightning-fast. Guofan and Hongzhang both favored encirclement, and Bingzhang strongly agreed. He broke the Nian south of Feng, Pei, and Suqian, pursued them to Cangjiaji, and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 又敗之淮南，長驅蒙城，捻西走，自此捻分東、西。

translations.literal: He defeated them again in Huainan, drove deep to Mengcheng, and the Nian fled west; from then on the Nian were divided into eastern and western groups.
translations.idiomatic: He beat them again in Huainan, drove deep to Mengcheng, and sent the Nian fleeing west—the moment when the movement split into eastern and western wings.

sentences.zh: 國籓令秉璋軍豫西，專剿東捻，與提督劉鼎勳俱。

translations.literal: Guofan ordered Bingzhang's army into western Henan to specialize in suppressing the eastern Nian, together with Provincial Commander Liu Dingxun.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan sent Bingzhang into western Henan with Provincial Commander Liu Dingxun to hunt the eastern Nian.

sentences.zh: 其冬，追入鄂。

translations.literal: That winter he pursued into Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he pursued them into Hubei.

sentences.zh: 六年，除山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed provincial treasurer of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made provincial treasurer of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 未上，捻自孝感小河溪竄河口鎮，與鼎勳軍追之，勳軍前鋒遇伏，總兵張遵道戰死，勢益熾，秉璋橫截之，始奔豫。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, the Nian fled from Xiaohexi in Xiaogan to Hekou town; with Dingxun's army he pursued them; the vanguard of Dingxun's army met an ambush and Brigadier Zhang Zundao died in battle; the rebels' momentum grew fiercer; Bingzhang cut across and blocked them, and only then did they flee toward Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office, the Nian slipped from Xiaohexi in Xiaogan to Hekou. Pursuing with Dingxun's force, he found Dingxun's vanguard ambushed and Brigadier Zhang Zundao killed. The rebels surged forward until Bingzhang cut across their path and drove them back toward Henan.

sentences.zh: 七年，鴻章代國籓督師，議扼運蹙捻海隅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Hongzhang replaced Guofan in commanding the army and proposed blocking the Grand Canal to drive the Nian into a corner by the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Hongzhang replaced Guofan as commander and proposed pinning the Nian against the coast by blocking the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 秉璋駐運西，捻撲濰河，將自沂、莒窺江淮。

translations.literal: Bingzhang was stationed west of the canal; the Nian rushed the Wei River and were about to spy out the Jianghuai region from Yi and Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang held the west bank of the canal while the Nian struck the Wei River, threatening to break through Yi and Ju toward the Jianghuai heartland.

sentences.zh: 秉璋亟渡河詣桃源，會浙軍扼清江。

translations.literal: Bingzhang urgently crossed the river and went to Taoyuan, just as the Zhejiang army blocked Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang hurried across the river toward Taoyuan, only to find the Zhejiang army already holding Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 亡何，賴酋率殘騎數千至，追破之淮城。

translations.literal: Before long, the Lai chieftain led several thousand remnant horsemen there; he pursued and defeated them at Huai city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the Lai chieftain arrived with several thousand remnant cavalry; Bingzhang pursued and routed them at Huai city.

sentences.zh: 事寧，被賞賚。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended, he was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: On his father's death he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起江西布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was recalled as Jiangxi provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed provincial treasurer of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu (1875) he was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 以母老再乞終養。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he again petitioned to retire and care for her until her death.
translations.idiomatic: His mother being advanced in years, he again asked leave to retire and support her for life.

sentences.zh: 六年，遭喪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he suffered a bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he went into mourning.

sentences.zh: 至九年，再起撫浙。

translations.literal: By the ninth year he was again appointed governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was recalled to serve as governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 會法越構釁，緣海戒嚴，秉璋躬履鎮海，令緣岸築長牆，置地雷，悉所有兵輪五艘，輔以紅單師船，據險設防。

translations.literal: Just then the Franco-Vietnamese conflict broke out; the coast was placed on alert. Bingzhang went in person to Zhenhai and ordered long walls built along the shore, land mines laid, all five gunboats deployed, and red-boat merchant vessels added to hold the passes and set defenses.
translations.idiomatic: War with France in Vietnam broke out, and the coast was put on alert. Bingzhang went personally to Zhenhai, ordered long walls built along the shore and land mines planted, deployed all five gunboats at his disposal, reinforced them with red-boat merchant vessels, and fortified every strategic point.

sentences.zh: 十一年，法艦入蛟門，令守備吳杰轟拒之，傷其三艘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year French warships entered Jiaomen; he ordered the garrison commander Wu Jie to drive them off with cannon fire and damage three of their ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year French warships entered Jiaomen. He ordered Garrison Commander Wu Jie to repel them with artillery and three of their ships were damaged.

sentences.zh: 越數日，復入虎蹲山北，再敗之，法將迷祿中砲死。

translations.literal: Several days later they entered again north of Hudun Mountain; he defeated them again, and the French general Mire was killed by a cannon shot.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the French returned north of Hudun Mountain and were beaten again; the French general Mire was killed by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 然猶浮小舟潛窺南岸，復令總兵錢玉興隱卒清泉嶺下突擊之，敵兵多赴水死。

translations.literal: Yet they still floated small boats to spy secretly on the south bank; he again ordered Brigadier Qian Yuxing to hide troops below Qingquan Ridge and strike suddenly; many enemy soldiers died in the water.
translations.idiomatic: They still sent small boats to reconnoiter the south bank in secret. Bingzhang again ordered Brigadier Qian Yuxing to ambush them from Qingquan Ridge; many of the enemy drowned trying to escape.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，擢四川總督。

translations.literal: After a year he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 川境窵遠，外接番、夷，內叢姦宄。

translations.literal: The Sichuan border was vast and remote; outside it adjoined frontier tribes and barbarians, and within it swarmed treacherous villains.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's territory was vast and remote, bordered on the outside by frontier tribes and on the inside by clusters of outlaws.

sentences.zh: 秉璋曰：「盜賊蠻夷，何代蔑有？

translations.literal: Bingzhang said: "Bandits and barbarian tribes—what age has ever lacked them?
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang said, "Bandits and frontier tribes—what dynasty has ever been without them?

sentences.zh: 以重兵臨之，幸而勝，不為武；

translations.literal: To confront them with heavy troops and, if fortunate, win—this is not true martial prowess;
translations.idiomatic: To crush them with overwhelming force and, if you are lucky, win—that is not real strength;

sentences.zh: 不幸而不勝，餉械轉資寇，是真不可為矣。」

translations.literal: if unlucky and defeated, pay and weapons turn to supply the bandits—that is truly what must not be done."
translations.idiomatic: and if you lose, your supplies and arms only feed the enemy—that is what truly must not be done."

sentences.zh: 故督蜀八年，歷平萬縣、茂州、川北、秀山土寇，其大小涼山、拉布浪、瞻對各夷畔服靡恆，則用趙營平屯田法，數月間皆慴伏，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Therefore, governing Shu for eight years, he successively pacified local bandits in Wan County, Maozhou, northern Sichuan, and Xiushan; for the various tribes of Greater and Lesser Liangshan, Labulang, and Zhandui, whose submission and rebellion were never constant, he applied Zhao Yingping's colonization method, and within months all were awed into submission; he was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, during eight years as governor of Sichuan he pacified local bandits in Wan County, Maozhou, northern Sichuan, and Xiushan. For the tribes of Greater and Lesser Liangshan, Labulang, and Zhandui, whose loyalty shifted constantly between rebellion and submission, he applied Zhao Yingping's frontier colonization method; within months all were subdued. He was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 御史鍾德祥劾提督錢玉興及道員葉毓榮不職狀，事下湖北巡撫譚繼洵，廉得實，秉璋坐濫舉罪罷。

translations.literal: Censor Zhong Dexiang impeached Brigadier Qian Yuxing and Circuit Intendant Ye Yurong for dereliction; the case was sent down to Hubei Governor Tan Jixun, who investigated and found the charges true; Bingzhang was dismissed for the crime of improper recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhong Dexiang impeached Brigadier Qian Yuxing and Circuit Intendant Ye Yurong for neglect of duty. The case was referred to Hubei Governor Tan Jixun, who confirmed it. Bingzhang was dismissed for having recommended them improperly.

sentences.zh: 初，丁寶楨督蜀，稱弊絕風清。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ding Baozhen governed Shu, it was said that corruption was eliminated and the wind was pure.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ding Baozhen governed Sichuan, the province was praised as utterly free of corruption.

sentences.zh: 秉璋承其後，難為繼，故世多病之。

translations.literal: Bingzhang succeeded him and found it hard to follow; hence the world often faulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang followed him and could not match his record, so contemporaries often criticized him.

sentences.zh: 未受代而民教相閧，重慶先有教案，秉璋初至，捕教民羅元義、亂民石匯等寘之法。

translations.literal: Before his successor arrived, conflict erupted between the people and the missionaries; Chongqing had already had a missionary case; when Bingzhang first arrived, he arrested the Christian convert Luo Yuanyi, the rioter Shi Hui, and others and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Before his successor could take over, clashes between locals and missionaries broke out. Chongqing had already seen a missionary incident, and when Bingzhang first arrived he arrested the Christian convert Luo Yuanyi, the rioter Shi Hui, and others and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 至是各屬繼起，教堂被毀者數十，教士忿，牒總署，指名奪秉璋職。

translations.literal: At this time incidents arose in succession in the subordinate districts; dozens of churches were destroyed; the missionaries were enraged, memorialized the general office, and named Bingzhang to be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Then similar outbreaks spread through the subordinate districts; dozens of churches were destroyed. The missionaries, furious, petitioned the legation and demanded Bingzhang's removal by name.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，許之，秉璋遂歸。

translations.literal: The court, having no choice, granted the request, and Bingzhang then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The court, unable to refuse, agreed, and Bingzhang went home.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he died.

sentences.zh: 總督周馥及蘇紳惲彥彬等先後上其功，复官，予優恤，建祠。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhou Fu and Jiangsu gentry Yun Yanbin and others successively submitted memorials on his merits; his office was restored, generous posthumous honors were granted, and a shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhou Fu and Jiangsu gentry such as Yun Yanbin successively memorialized the throne on his behalf. His rank was restored, generous posthumous honors were granted, and a shrine was erected.

sentences.zh: 陳士杰，字俊丞，湖南桂陽州人。

translations.literal: Chen Shijie, courtesy name Juncheng, was a native of Guiyang Prefecture in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shijie, styled Juncheng, came from Guiyang Prefecture in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢考取小京官，銓戶部，與閻敬銘同曹司，並以戇樸稱。

translations.literal: Through the selected tribute-student examination he gained appointment as a minor capital official and was assigned to the Board of Revenue; he served in the same bureau as Yan Jingming, and both were known for blunt plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a tribute student, he passed the examination for minor capital posts and was assigned to the Board of Revenue, where he served alongside Yan Jingming; both were known for blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，歸。

translations.literal: On his father's death he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 值粵寇亂，土匪竊發，集團勇得百餘人，平之。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels were in rebellion, local bandits rose in secret; he gathered militia of more than a hundred men and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping rebellion local bandits broke out; he raised a militia of more than a hundred men and put them down.

sentences.zh: 俄白水奸民陷永桂，新田告急，眾議拒之。
