translations.literal: Soon Baishui ruffians seized Yonggui; Xintian sent urgent appeals for help, and the assembly debated refusing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon ruffians from Baishui overran Yonggui. Xintian sent urgent appeals for aid, but the local leaders debated whether to refuse.

sentences.zh: 士傑曰：「援新田乃所以自保也！」

translations.literal: Shijie said: "To aid Xintian is precisely how to protect ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Shijie said, "Helping Xintian is how we protect ourselves!"

sentences.zh: 越境擊卻之。

translations.literal: He crossed the border and struck, driving them back.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the border, attacked, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓治軍衡州，闢參戎幕。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan raised an army at Hengzhou, he was invited to join the military staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan mustered troops at Hengzhou, Shijie was invited to join his staff.

sentences.zh: 鮑超時為小校，坐法當斬，​​力請釋之。

translations.literal: Bao Chao was then a junior officer; having violated the law he was liable to execution, and Shijie forcefully pleaded for his release.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chao was then a junior officer condemned to death for a military offense; Shijie pleaded forcefully for his release.

sentences.zh: 從援湖北，壁岳州城外，王珍軍次蒲圻，違國籓誡，敗退，入空城死守，國籓憤甚，將士莫敢為言，士傑獨請赴救，弗應，固請之，曰：「救之如何？」

translations.literal: Following the relief of Hubei, they encamped outside Yuezhou city; Wang Zhen's army was stationed at Puqi, disobeyed Guofan's orders, was defeated and retreated, and entered an empty city to hold out to the death. Guofan was furious; officers and soldiers dared not speak for Wang, but Shijie alone asked to go to the rescue. Guofan did not agree; Shijie pressed the request, and Guofan said: "How should we save him?"
translations.idiomatic: On the Hubei relief campaign they encamped outside Yuezhou. Wang Zhen's force, stationed at Puqi, defied Guofan's orders, was beaten back, and shut itself in an empty town to make a last stand. Guofan was furious; no officer dared speak for Wang, but Shijie alone asked to go to his rescue. Guofan refused until Shijie pressed again, and Guofan asked, "Then how would you save him?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「寇無戰船，宜遣水師傍岸舉砲為聲援。」

translations.literal: Shijie said: "The rebels have no war junks; we should send the river force along the bank to fire cannon as a supporting demonstration."
translations.idiomatic: Shijie replied, "The rebels have no war junks. Send the river force along the bank to fire cannon in support."

sentences.zh: 珍因獲免於難，厥後鮑、王並為名將。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen was thus spared disaster; afterward both Bao and Wang became famous generals.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen was saved. Later both Bao and Wang became celebrated generals.

sentences.zh: 岳州既敗，寇遂略湘陰，陸走寧鄉，水斷靖港，進陷湘潭據之。

translations.literal: Once Yuezhou was lost, the rebels then overran Xiangyin, marched overland to Ningxiang, cut off Jinggang by water, advanced and captured Xiangtan, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuezhou fell, the rebels overran Xiangyin, marched overland toward Ningxiang, blocked Jinggang by river, and advanced to seize Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 國籓水師頓湘川，去寧鄉、靖港皆數十里。

translations.literal: Guofan's river force halted at Xiangchuan, several tens of li from both Ningxiang and Jinggang.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan's river force lay idle at Xiangchuan, dozens of li from both Ningxiang and Jinggang.

sentences.zh: 或請守省城，或請絕津迳奪寇艎，議未決。

translations.literal: Some urged holding the provincial capital, others urged cutting off the river route to seize the rebels' war junks; no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged defending the provincial capital; others proposed cutting the river route and seizing the rebel junks. No decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 士傑謂宜援湘潭，即不利，猶得保衡、永，圖再舉。

translations.literal: Shijie said they should relieve Xiangtan; even if things went badly, they could still hold Hengzhou and Yongzhou and plan another effort.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie argued they should relieve Xiangtan: even if the attempt failed, they could still hold Hengzhou and Yongzhou and regroup.

sentences.zh: 國籓如其言，果大捷。

translations.literal: Guofan followed his advice and indeed won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan took his advice and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 論功，遷主事。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, he was promoted to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋歸省，復出佐糧運。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on leave, then went out again to assist with grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home on leave, then returned to assist with grain transport.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，永、桂土匪起，聞亂，單舸溯江歸，專治團練。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, bandits rose in Yongzhou and Guiyang; hearing of the disturbance, he returned alone by boat upriver and devoted himself to organizing militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianfeng bandits broke out in Yongzhou and Guiyang. Hearing of the trouble, he sailed upriver alone and devoted himself to organizing local militia.

sentences.zh: 亡何，連州匪構嶺南北奸民，眾十萬，陷郴州。

translations.literal: Before long, Lianzhou bandits joined with ruffians north and south of the ranges; their force reached a hundred thousand and they captured Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lianzhou rebels joined with ruffians north and south of the Nanling ranges; their force swelled to a hundred thousand and they took Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 與珍會師擊之，復其城，遂以南防屬之。

translations.literal: He joined forces with Wang Zhen to attack them, recovered the city, and then entrusted southern defense to him.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Wang Zhen, drove the rebels out, and recovered the city, then put him in charge of the southern defense.

sentences.zh: 留州賦充餉，改團為營，號廣武軍。

translations.literal: He retained the prefecture's tax revenues for pay, converted the militia into battalions, and named the force the Guangwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the prefecture's tax revenues for supplies, converted the militia into regular battalions, and called the force the Guangwu Army.

sentences.zh: 永、郴、桂陽邊地千里，廣武當其衝，數挫寇鋒，而以捍石達開功為盛。

translations.literal: The borderlands of Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guiyang stretched a thousand li; Guangwu stood in their path and repeatedly blunted the rebels' spearhead, its greatest fame coming from blocking Shi Dakai.
translations.idiomatic: Across a thousand li of borderland in Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guiyang, the Guangwu Army stood in the path of invasion, repeatedly blunting rebel attacks; its greatest fame came from holding back Shi Dakai.

sentences.zh: 達開故黠猾，麾下號百萬，分七部，能檢勒之使毋擾。

translations.literal: Dakai was by nature cunning and slippery; his followers were said to number a million, divided into seven divisions, yet he could restrain them and keep them from plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai was famously cunning; his followers were said to number a million in seven divisions, yet he could restrain them from looting.

sentences.zh: 九年春，自贛而西，至桂陽，穿城北走。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he came west from Jiangxi to Guiyang and passed north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he marched west from Jiangxi to Guiyang and passed north of the city.

sentences.zh: 時廣武軍軍花園砦，有橋跨鍾水，曰鬥下渡，其南兩山相崟，一迳中達，東西北皆環水。

translations.literal: At the time the Guangwu Army was encamped at Huayuan Stockade; a bridge crossed the Zhong River at Douxia Ford; south of it two mountains faced each other steeply, with a single path running between them; east, west, and north were all ringed by water.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangwu Army was then encamped at Huayuan Stockade. A bridge crossed the Zhong River at Douxia Ford; south of it two mountains rose steeply on either side of a single path, while water ringed the position on the east, west, and north.

sentences.zh: 士傑遣一裨將領百人扼橋，寇夜至，大驚，不敢前。

translations.literal: Shijie sent a lieutenant with a hundred men to hold the bridge; the rebels arrived at night, were greatly alarmed, and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie sent a lieutenant with a hundred men to hold the bridge. The rebels arrived at night, were thrown into panic, and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 後來者欲退則隘塞，欲旁出則無路。

translations.literal: Those who came later wished to retreat but the pass was blocked; they wished to break out sideways but there was no way.
translations.idiomatic: Those behind wanted to retreat but the pass was jammed; they tried to break out to the sides but found no escape.

sentences.zh: 平明，士傑率師轟擊之，自相蹈藉，墜死無算。

translations.literal: At daybreak Shijie led his force in a cannon barrage; they trampled one another, and those who fell to their deaths were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Shijie opened fire with his main force. The rebels trampled one another in the crush; countless men fell to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 是役也，士傑以數百人敗寇數十萬眾，達開襲省之計卒無所施，上嘉之，擢知府。

translations.literal: In this battle Shijie with several hundred men defeated a rebel force of several hundred thousand; Dakai's plan to strike the provincial capital came to nothing; the throne commended him and promoted him to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle Shijie with a few hundred men routed a rebel host said to number in the tens of thousands, foiling Dakai's plan to strike the provincial capital. The throne praised him and promoted him to prefect.

sentences.zh: 嗣錄援藍山、嘉禾、寧遠功，晉道員。

translations.literal: Later his merits in relieving Lanshan, Jiahe, and Ningyuan were recorded, and he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: His service in relieving Lanshan, Jiahe, and Ningyuan was later recognized, and he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，三吳軍事棘，以國籓薦，超授江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi the military situation in the Three Wu region was critical; on Guofan's recommendation he was exceptionally appointed Jiangsu judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi the war in the lower Yangzi region was desperate. On Guofan's recommendation he was appointed Jiangsu judicial commissioner out of turn.

sentences.zh: 士傑慮石黨往來郴、永貽母憂，乞終養，以防遏上游為己任，數卻寇。

translations.literal: Shijie feared that Shi's followers moving between Chenzhou and Yongzhou would distress his mother; he petitioned to retire and care for her, took blocking the upper reaches as his own duty, and repeatedly repelled the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie feared that Shi's forces moving between Chenzhou and Yongzhou would worry his mother, so he asked leave to retire and care for her, making it his duty to hold the upper reaches and repeatedly driving the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 四年，論功，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when merits were assessed, he was given the rank of provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was granted the rank of provincial treasurer for his service.

sentences.zh: 時江南既定，而霆軍所降寇复叛，自湖北金田入郴，數千里無與逆戰者。

translations.literal: At the time the lower Yangzi had been pacified, but bandits surrendered by the Ting Army rebelled again, entered Chenzhou from Jintian in Hubei, and for several thousand li no one met them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangzi had been pacified, but rebels surrendered by the Ting Army rose again, marching from Jintian in Hubei into Chenzhou; for thousands of li no one stood to fight them.

sentences.zh: 士傑要擊之，寇大潰，賜號剛勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Shijie intercepted them; the rebels were utterly routed, and he was granted the title Gangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie intercepted them and the rebels were routed. He received the title Gangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 十年，母喪，服闋，除山東按察使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year his mother died; when mourning ended he was appointed Shandong judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his mother died. After mourning he was appointed judicial commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，到官，多所平反。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he took office and reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he took office and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 晉福建布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Fujian provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial treasurer of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 未上，會巡撫文格被劾，詞連士傑，罷免。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, Governor Wenge was impeached; the charges implicated Shijie, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office, Governor Wenge was impeached in a case that implicated Shijie, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋以台灣軍務，命署福建按察使。

translations.literal: Soon, because of the Taiwan military situation, he was ordered to serve as acting Fujian judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, with Taiwan in crisis, he was appointed acting judicial commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢撫浙江。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 巡海口，增築鎮海笠山港及定海乍浦砲台。

translations.literal: He inspected the seaports and added fortifications at Zhenhai's Lishan Port and Dinghai's Zhapu batteries.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the coastal defenses and added batteries at Lishan Port in Zhenhai and Zhapu in Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 八年，移山東，緣海設防。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shandong and set up coastal defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shandong to organize coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 吳大澂會辦北洋防務，至登州、煙台，見廣武軍壁壘，頗採其法而增損之，奏請頒行各海口。

translations.literal: Wu Dacheng jointly managed Beiyang coastal defense; when he reached Dengzhou and Yantai and saw the Guangwu Army's fortifications, he largely adopted their methods with modifications and memorialized that they be issued to every seaport.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dacheng, overseeing Beiyang coastal defense, visited Dengzhou and Yantai, inspected the Guangwu Army's fortifications, adapted their methods with improvements, and memorialized that the design be adopted at every port.

sentences.zh: 而忌者中以蜚語，至劾其海防草率，事下尚書延煦、左都御史祁世長，得白。

translations.literal: But jealous men spread slander until he was impeached for careless coastal defense; the case was sent down to Minister Yan Xu and Censor-in-Chief Qi Shichang, and he was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Envious rivals spread rumors until he was impeached for slipshod coastal defense. The case went to Minister Yan Xu and Censor-in-Chief Qi Shichang, who cleared him.

sentences.zh: 海防軍罷，而士傑亦病矣，數請乞休，始允。

translations.literal: The coastal defense force was disbanded, and Shijie also fell ill; he repeatedly petitioned to retire, and only then was permission granted.
translations.idiomatic: The coastal defense force was disbanded. Shijie had also fallen ill and repeatedly asked to retire; at last his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒於家，予省城及本籍建祠。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died at home; shrines were granted in the provincial capital and his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he died at home. Shrines were erected in the provincial capital and in his native district.

sentences.zh: 陶模，字方之，浙江秀水人。

translations.literal: Tao Mo, courtesy name Fangzhi, was a native of Xiushui in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Mo, styled Fangzhi, came from Xiushui in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 同治七年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the seventh year of Tongzhi, he was selected for the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Tongzhi and entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 散館，授甘肅文縣知縣，調皋蘭。

translations.literal: After completing his Hanlin probation he was appointed magistrate of Wen County in Gansu and transferred to Gaolan.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin probation he was appointed magistrate of Wen County in Gansu, then transferred to Gaolan.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠為總督，方徵回，又創建貢院，兵工諸役並作，模躬自料量，民不知擾。

translations.literal: When Zuo Zongtang was governor-general, the campaign to recover the northwest was underway and an examination hall was also being built; military and construction projects proceeded together, yet Mo personally measured and calculated the work, and the people were unaware of disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: While Zuo Zongtang was governor-general, the northwest campaign was underway and a new examination hall was being built; military and construction projects ran in parallel. Mo personally supervised the measurements and scheduling, and the people scarcely felt the burden.

sentences.zh: 遷秦州直隸州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qinzhou Direct Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qinzhou Direct Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，流徙饑民數十萬麕集，出積俸，並割公使銀四萬餘金設粥廠，不足，貸金益之。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, several hundred thousand displaced starving people gathered in crowds; he disbursed his accumulated salary and also cut more than forty thousand taels from public funds to set up gruel kitchens; when that was insufficient, he borrowed money to increase the relief.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year several hundred thousand starving refugees gathered. He spent his saved salary and more than forty thousand taels from public funds to open soup kitchens; when that was not enough, he borrowed still more.

sentences.zh: 修養濟院，增義田，卹嫠婦。

translations.literal: He repaired the poor-relief hospice, increased the charity fields, and gave relief to widows.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the poor-relief hospice, expanded the charity fields, and provided for widows.

sentences.zh: 州南藉水齧城堙，模為築堤沼三百五十丈，植芙蕖楊柳，蓄鱗介，取其利，以時繕完。

translations.literal: South of the prefecture the Jieshui River gnawed at the city walls and buried them; Mo built dikes and ponds three hundred and fifty zhang long, planted lotus and willows, stocked fish and shellfish, took their profit, and repaired them in season.
translations.idiomatic: South of the prefecture the Jieshui River was eroding and burying the city walls. Mo built dikes and ponds three hundred and fifty zhang long, planted lotus and willows, stocked them with fish, used the revenue for upkeep, and kept the works in repair.

sentences.zh: 署甘州府知府，罷屬縣供億。

translations.literal: Acting as prefect of Ganzhou Prefecture, he abolished the lodging and supply levies on subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: As acting prefect of Ganzhou he abolished the lodging and supply levies imposed on subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 宗棠奏模治行第一，調補迪化州。

translations.literal: Zongtang memorialized that Mo's administrative conduct ranked first and had him transferred to fill the post at Dihua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang reported Mo's administration the best in the province and had him transferred to Dihua.

sentences.zh: 編修廖壽豐薦模器識宏遠，堪備閫寄。

translations.literal: Compiler Liao Shoufeng recommended Mo for his broad vision and capacity, saying he was fit to bear military command.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Liao Shoufeng recommended Mo for his breadth of vision and judged him fit for high military responsibility.

sentences.zh: 時回久亂，民戶寥落，模和輯漢、回，耕者復聚。

translations.literal: At the time the Hui had long been in turmoil and households were sparse; Mo reconciled Han and Hui, and farmers gathered again to cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: The region had long been torn by Hui unrest and its population was depleted. Mo reconciled Han and Hui communities, and farmers began to return.

sentences.zh: 時議定賦則，模謂經畫窮塞，當通周官一易再易之義，令民以二畝當一畝，徵其六緩其四。

translations.literal: At the time land-tax rates were being fixed; Mo said that in planning for remote frontier regions one should apply the meaning of the Rites of Zhou's one-renewal and two-renewal system, letting the people count two mu as one mu, collecting six parts and deferring four.
translations.idiomatic: As land-tax rates were being set, Mo argued that frontier settlement should follow the Rites of Zhou principle of graded land renewal: let two mu count as one for taxation, collecting six-tenths now and deferring four.

sentences.zh: 宗棠採其議，邊民始有久居志。

translations.literal: Zongtang adopted his proposal, and the frontier people first gained the will to settle for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang adopted his proposal, and the frontier people at last began to think of staying for good.

sentences.zh: 歷署蘭州府、蘭州道、按察使，調直隸按察使、陝西布政使，護巡撫。

translations.literal: He successively served as acting prefect of Lanzhou, Lanzhou circuit intendant, and judicial commissioner; was transferred to judicial commissioner of Zhili and provincial treasurer of Shaanxi; and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as acting prefect of Lanzhou, Lanzhou circuit intendant, and judicial commissioner, then was transferred to judicial commissioner of Zhili and provincial treasurer of Shaanxi, where he also acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 而俄兵在帕米爾，意叵測。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Russian troops were in the Pamirs, and their intentions were hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Russian troops were in the Pamirs, and their intentions were impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 模以邊防無效，自請罷斥，不允。

translations.literal: Mo, believing frontier defense ineffective, asked to be dismissed; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Believing frontier defense had failed, Mo asked to be removed from office; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 廷議將以帕米爾為三國甌脫，英垂諾，俄猶不可，陳兵相持。

translations.literal: The court debated making the Pamirs a neutral zone among three nations; Britain seemed to agree, but Russia still would not accept, and both sides massed troops in confrontation.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated making the Pamirs a neutral zone among three powers. Britain seemed willing, but Russia would not agree, and both sides massed troops in a standoff.

sentences.zh: 模取德意志兵法練邊軍，選幼童百餘，課以測算諸法，將徐推之各軍。

translations.literal: Mo took German military manuals to train the frontier army, selected more than a hundred young boys, drilled them in surveying and calculation methods, and planned gradually to extend this to every army.
translations.idiomatic: Mo trained the frontier army on German military manuals, selected more than a hundred boys, taught them surveying and calculation, and planned to extend the program to every unit.

sentences.zh: 見將佐必以惜勞苦、寶槍彈為戒。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw officers he always admonished them to spare the men hardship and treasure gun and ammunition.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he addressed his officers he warned them to spare their men hardship and to treat ammunition as precious.

sentences.zh: 初，俄人借巴爾魯克山以處所屬哈薩克，期十年。

translations.literal: Earlier the Russians had borrowed Mount Baluk to settle their Kazakhs there, for a term of ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Russia had been lent Mount Baluk to settle its Kazakhs there for a term of ten years.

sentences.zh: 山饒水泉林木，當塔城西北，廣袤數百里。

translations.literal: The mountain was rich in springs, water, and timber; it lay northwest of Tacheng and extended several hundred li in breadth.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain was rich in springs and timber, lay northwest of Tacheng, and covered several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 至是期滿，無還意。

translations.literal: When the term expired, they had no intention of returning it.
translations.idiomatic: When the term expired, they showed no intention of giving it back.

sentences.zh: 模爭之，逾年乃如約。

translations.literal: Mo disputed it; only after more than a year was the agreement honored.
translations.idiomatic: Mo pressed the issue, and only after more than a year was the agreement honored.

sentences.zh: 俄商及附英諸部至新疆皆不稅。

translations.literal: Russian merchants and tribes attached to Britain who came to Xinjiang paid no tax at all.
translations.idiomatic: Russian merchants and British-affiliated tribes entering Xinjiang paid no taxes at all.

sentences.zh: 模曰：「是獨苦吾民！」

translations.literal: Mo said: "This alone burdens our people!
translations.idiomatic: Mo said, "This alone burdens our people!"

sentences.zh: 為奏請普免焉。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking for universal exemption.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that the exemption be made universal.

sentences.zh: 纏回文字語言不相通，漢民愚之，貸金輒取重息，至賣鬻妻子以償。

translations.literal: The Taranchi script and language did not match; Han people cheated them, charging heavy interest on loans until they sold wives and children to repay.
translations.idiomatic: The Taranchi script and language differed from those of the Han, whom they did not understand; Han lenders charged usurious interest until borrowers sold wives and children to repay their debts.

sentences.zh: 模為之規定章條，令讀書習漢語，於是回族欣欣向化矣。

translations.literal: Mo drew up regulations for them, ordered study of books and Chinese speech, and thereafter the Hui communities gladly turned toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Mo issued regulations requiring literacy and the study of Chinese, and thereafter the Hui communities gladly accepted civilization.

sentences.zh: 羅布淖爾，古蒲昌海也，荒沙無垠，亙新疆中部。

translations.literal: Lop Nur is the ancient Puchang Sea: boundless desert sand spanning the center of Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lop Nur, the ancient Puchang Sea, is an expanse of desert sand without limit, stretching across central Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 模議闢徑路，自新疆之南，青海、西藏之北，噶斯、烏蘭達布遜、阿耨達、托古茲尼蟒依諸大雪山之陰，迂迴出入，分道測繪，得金鐵煤諸礦數十百計，欲開採利民，以絀於貲，工不克舉。

translations.literal: Mo proposed opening a direct route from south of Xinjiang and north of Qinghai and Tibet, along the northern slopes of the great snow mountains Gas, Ulan Dabuxun, Anmoda, and Toguznihmanyi, entering and leaving by winding paths, surveying in separate parties, and found dozens or hundreds of gold, iron, and coal mines; he wished to open them for the people's benefit, but for lack of funds the work could not be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Mo proposed opening a direct route south of Xinjiang and north of Qinghai and Tibet, along the northern slopes of the great snow ranges of Gas, Ulan Dabuxun, Anmoda, and Toguznihmanyi. Parties surveyed the winding approaches separately and identified scores of gold, iron, and coal deposits. He wished to develop them for public benefit, but funds ran short and the project could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 乃於羅布淖爾北四百餘裡築蒲昌城，南百四十里設屯防局，回民徙居成村落。

translations.literal: He therefore built Puchang City more than four hundred li north of Lop Nur and established a garrison bureau one hundred and forty li to the south; Hui settlers moved in and formed villages.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore built Puchang City more than four hundred li north of Lop Nur and established a garrison bureau one hundred and forty li farther south; Hui settlers moved in and formed villages.

sentences.zh: 其後設置營縣，實自模開之。

translations.literal: The later establishment of camps and counties in fact began with Mo.
translations.idiomatic: The later establishment of military camps and counties in the region began with Mo.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日本略朝鮮，朝議決戰，師屢敗。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Japan encroached on Korea; the court decided on war and the army was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Japan encroached on Korea; the court resolved on war, and the army was repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 甘肅提督董福祥先以祝嘏在京，募兵備戰，河湟回族聞亂思蠢動。

translations.literal: Gansu military governor Dong Fuxiang had earlier come to the capital for birthday congratulations, recruited troops to prepare for war, and the Hehuang Hui, hearing of the disorder, thought of rising.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu military governor Dong Fuxiang had come to the capital for birthday congratulations and was recruiting troops for war when the Hehuang Hui, hearing of the turmoil, began to stir.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，撒拉河州、西寧、大通諸回先後反。

translations.literal: In spring of the twenty-first year the Salar at Hezhou, Xining, Datong, and other Hui successively rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-first year the Salar at Hezhou and the Hui of Xining, Datong, and other places rose in succession.

sentences.zh: 西寧回酋劉四伏尤悍，模遣將援巴燕戎格，與總督楊昌濬合疏請命福祥帥師西援。

translations.literal: Liu Sifu, Hui chieftain at Xining, was especially fierce; Mo sent generals to aid Bayan Rongge and jointly memorialized with Governor-General Yang Changjun requesting that Fuxiang lead troops west to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sifu, the Hui chieftain at Xining, was especially fierce. Mo sent generals to relieve Bayan Rongge and, together with Governor-General Yang Changjun, memorialized asking that Fuxiang be ordered to lead troops west in support.

sentences.zh: 夏，平番回亦變，河西諸府東不能通省會，則西乞援新疆。

translations.literal: In summer the Pingfan Hui also rebelled; the prefectures west of the river could not reach the provincial capital to the east, so they begged aid from Xinjiang to the west.
translations.idiomatic: In summer the Pingfan Hui also rebelled. The prefectures west of the river could no longer reach the provincial capital to the east and turned west to beg aid from Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 模奏陳回亂日亟，部遣諸將羅平安戍哈密，牛允誠守安西、玉門，趙有正屯肅州，而於哈密置東防營務處，以道員潘效蘇護諸將。

translations.literal: Mo memorialized that the Hui rebellion grew daily urgent; the ministry dispatched generals—Luo Ping'an garrisoned Hami, Niu Yuncheng held Anxi and Yumen, Zhao Youzheng encamped at Suzhou—and at Hami established an Eastern Defense Camp Affairs Office, with circuit intendant Pan Xiaosu to coordinate the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Mo reported that the Hui rebellion was growing daily more urgent. The ministry dispatched generals: Luo Ping'an garrisoned Hami, Niu Yuncheng held Anxi and Yumen, and Zhao Youzheng encamped at Suzhou. At Hami an Eastern Defense Camp Affairs Office was established, with circuit intendant Pan Xiaosu to coordinate the commanders.

sentences.zh: 諸亂回遣其徒出關煽新疆回部。

translations.literal: The rebel Hui sent their followers out of the pass to incite the Hui of Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Hui sent their followers beyond the frontier pass to stir up the Hui communities of Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 九月，綏來回發難，以有備，旋定。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Suilai Hui rose; because preparations had been made, it was quickly settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Suilai Hui rose in revolt, but because defenses were ready the disturbance was quickly put down.

sentences.zh: 迪化回應之，模诇知莠民與牙役密相結，捕斬六人而亂弭。

translations.literal: The Dihua Hui responded; Mo learned that ruffians were secretly allied with petty officials, captured and executed six men, and the turmoil subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The Dihua Hui responded in turn. Mo discovered that ruffians were in secret league with petty officials, captured and executed six men, and the unrest was quelled.

sentences.zh: 十月，回逼甘州，上罷昌濬，以模署陝甘總督，命入關剿撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Hui pressed Ganzhou; the emperor dismissed Changjun, had Mo act as governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu, and ordered him to enter the pass to suppress and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Hui pressed Ganzhou. The emperor dismissed Changjun, appointed Mo acting governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu, and ordered him into the pass to suppress and pacify the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時福祥將甘軍渡洮，魏光燾將湘軍臨湟水。

translations.literal: At the time Fuxiang was leading Gansu troops across the Tao River and Wei Guangtao was leading Hunan troops to the Huangshui.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fuxiang was leading Gansu troops across the Tao River while Wei Guangtao was bringing Hunan troops to the Huangshui.

sentences.zh: 模策東路兵大集，回且西竄，乃遣兵分駐天山北迪化、鎮西為中權，而繕完防禦天山以南諸要隘。

translations.literal: Mo calculated that eastern troops were massing and the Hui would flee west; he dispatched troops to garrison Dihua and Zhenxi north of the Tianshan as a central reserve while completing defenses at key passes south of the Tianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Mo judged that eastern forces were massing and the Hui would flee west. He posted troops at Dihua and Zhenxi north of the Tianshan as a central reserve and strengthened the defenses at key passes south of the range.

sentences.zh: 後路既設備，乃將馬步八營馳入關，道經沙漠至吐魯番城，回王瑪木特來會，勗以大義。

translations.literal: Once the rear was prepared, he led eight battalions of horse and foot into the pass at speed, traveling through desert to Turfan; the Hui king Mamut came to meet him and Mo exhorted him with righteous principle.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rear was secured, he led eight battalions of horse and foot through the pass at speed, crossing the desert to Turfan. The Hui king Mamut came to meet him, and Mo urged him with the claims of duty and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 至哈密，校閱各軍，令纏回與焉。

translations.literal: At Hami he reviewed the armies and had the Taranchi take part.
translations.idiomatic: At Hami he inspected the armies and included the Taranchi in the review.

sentences.zh: 模以有正兵寡，戒毋輕出。

translations.literal: Mo, because Youzheng's troops were few, warned him not to sally lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Because Youzheng's force was small, Mo warned him not to venture out rashly.

sentences.zh: 有正喜功，出攻察漢俄博、永安二城皆下。

translations.literal: Youzheng was eager for merit and sallied forth to attack Chahan Ebo and Yong'an; both cities fell.
translations.idiomatic: Youzheng, eager for glory, sallied out and attacked Chahan Ebo and Yong'an; both cities fell.

sentences.zh: 二十二年元夕，薄北大通營，敗歸。

translations.literal: On the New Year's Eve of the twenty-second year he approached the northern Datong Camp and returned defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve of the twenty-second year he advanced on the northern Datong Camp and returned in defeat.

sentences.zh: 模遣涼州戍軍赴援。

translations.literal: Mo sent garrison troops from Liangzhou to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Mo sent the Liangzhou garrison to his relief.

sentences.zh: 二月，入關，群回斂聚山南，模至蘭州視事，令效蘇督諸將略北大通營，破所領十大莊堡，戮其酋，殲數千人，諸回氣奪。

translations.literal: In the second month he entered the pass; the Hui gathered south of the mountains. Mo reached Lanzhou to take office, ordered Xiaosu to supervise the generals in advancing on the northern Datong Camp, broke the ten large fortified villages under their leader, executed their chieftain, killed several thousand, and the Hui lost their fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he entered the pass. The Hui gathered south of the mountains. Mo reached Lanzhou to assume office and ordered Xiaosu to direct the generals against the northern Datong Camp. They stormed the ten large fortified villages under its leader, executed the chieftain, and killed several thousand men, and the Hui lost their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 會光燾亦定西寧，諸回自水峽口西竄青海。

translations.literal: About the same time Wei Guangtao also pacified Xining; the Hui fled west from Shuixia Pass into Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Wei Guangtao also pacified Xining, and the Hui fled west through Shuixia Pass into Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 模令效蘇等出塞，陳兵玉門諸山徑，毋縱賊出平地。

translations.literal: Mo ordered Xiaosu and others out of the frontier, arrayed troops along the mountain paths of Yumen, and forbade letting the bandits out onto open ground.
translations.idiomatic: Mo ordered Xiaosu and others beyond the frontier, posted troops along the mountain paths near Yumen, and forbade letting the rebels break out onto open ground.

sentences.zh: 青海蒙古積弱，久怵回悍，告急。

translations.literal: The Mongols of Qinghai had long been weak and for long feared the Hui's ferocity; they sent urgent appeals.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols of Qinghai had long been weak and had long feared the Hui for their fierceness; they sent urgent appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 朝議令光燾、福祥二軍追逐。

translations.literal: The court debated ordering Wei Guangtao and Fuxiang's two armies to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated ordering the armies of Wei Guangtao and Fuxiang to pursue.

sentences.zh: 模以師行絕域，糧芻車馱，重為民累，內地空虛，為禍滋大，奏寢其議。

translations.literal: Mo argued that troops marching into remote country, with grain and fodder carried by cart and pack animal, would heavily burden the people; the interior would be left empty and the harm would be greater; he memorialized to set aside the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Mo argued that sending troops into remote country, with grain and fodder hauled by cart and pack animal, would heavily burden the people, leave the interior empty, and make the harm even worse. He memorialized to set the proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 新疆將吏慮回更西竄，亦告急。

translations.literal: Xinjiang officers and officials, fearing the Hui would flee still farther west, also sent urgent appeals.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and officials of Xinjiang, fearing the Hui would flee still farther west, also sent urgent appeals.

sentences.zh: 朝議令提督鄧增出青海，張俊防北路。

translations.literal: The court debated ordering Military Governor Deng Zeng out from Qinghai and Zhang Jun to defend the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated ordering Military Governor Deng Zeng out from Qinghai and Zhang Jun to guard the northern route.

sentences.zh: 模策賊非至玉門、敦煌掠食，不能遽犯新疆，復請罷移軍議，而令增屯肅州為聲援。

translations.literal: Mo judged that the bandits could not suddenly invade Xinjiang unless they reached Yumen and Dunhuang to plunder food; he again asked to drop the plan to shift troops and had Zeng encamp at Suzhou as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Mo judged that the rebels could not suddenly invade Xinjiang unless they reached Yumen and Dunhuang to plunder supplies. He again asked that the plan to shift troops be dropped and had Zeng encamp at Suzhou as a supporting force.

sentences.zh: 光燾將湘軍還陝西，以與福祥不相能也。

translations.literal: Wei Guangtao led the Hunan army back to Shaanxi, because he and Fuxiang could not work together.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangtao led the Hunan army back to Shaanxi because he and Fuxiang could not cooperate.

sentences.zh: 賊自青海犯玉門，允誠等擊卻之。

translations.literal: The bandits from Qinghai attacked Yumen; Yuncheng and others beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels from Qinghai attacked Yumen, and Yuncheng and the others drove them back.

sentences.zh: 模令玉門軍赴安西。

translations.literal: Mo ordered the Yumen troops to proceed to Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Mo ordered the Yumen garrison to move to Anxi.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊大至，劉四伏奪路求食，諸將力戰，金蘭益匹馬陷陣，大敗賊於牛橋，降斬各數千人，飢凍死磧中者過半。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the bandits came in force; Liu Sifu fought his way through to find food; the generals fought hard, Jin Lanyi fell in battle at the head of a single horse; they routed the bandits at Niuchiao, capturing and killing several thousand each; more than half perished of hunger and cold in the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the rebels arrived in force. Liu Sifu fought his way through to find food. The generals battled fiercely; Jin Lanyi charged alone into the enemy line and was killed. At Niuchiao they routed the rebels, capturing and executing several thousand apiece, while more than half the remainder died of hunger and cold in the desert.

sentences.zh: 四伏以千數騎遁，中道伏發，就擒。

translations.literal: Sifu fled with about a thousand riders; an ambush was sprung mid-route and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu fled with about a thousand horsemen, but an ambush was sprung along the way and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 於是徙降回塔里木河濱，計口授田。

translations.literal: Thereupon the surrendered Hui were relocated along the Tarim River and given land by head count.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered Hui were then resettled along the Tarim River and allotted land according to the number of mouths in each household.

sentences.zh: 關內外悉平，論功，實授總督。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the pass were all pacified; for merit he was formally appointed governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the pass were fully pacified, and for his service he was formally appointed governor-general.

sentences.zh: 方日事之初起也，和戰議不決。

translations.literal: When the Japanese affair first arose, debate over peace and war was unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: When the conflict with Japan first broke out, the court could not decide between peace and war.

sentences.zh: 模言：「國強弱視人才，人才不足，和戰皆不足恃，即戰勝亦無益。」

translations.literal: Mo said: "Whether the state is strong or weak depends on talent; when talent is insufficient, neither peace nor war can be relied upon—even victory in war is of no use."
translations.idiomatic: Mo said, "A state's strength or weakness depends on talent. When talent is lacking, neither peace nor war can be trusted—even victory in war is useless."

sentences.zh: 因言：「天下事當變通者非一，如減中額，停捐例，汰冗員，令京官升遷不出本部，司員分類治事，刪棄舊案，破除旗兵積習，禁​​士大夫食鴉片，分設算學、藝學科目，廢武科，變操法，擇勳舊子弟遊學各國，培植工藝。

translations.literal: He went on to say: "Among affairs under heaven that need reform, there is more than one: such as reducing the metropolitan quota, stopping purchase offices, eliminating redundant posts, requiring capital officials not to be promoted outside their ministries, assigning clerks by category, discarding old cases, breaking the accumulated habits of banner troops, forbidding gentry and officials to use opium, establishing separate examinations in mathematics and technical arts, abolishing the military examination, changing drill methods, selecting sons of meritorious old families to study abroad, and nurturing craftsmanship.
translations.idiomatic: He continued, "More than one thing in the empire needs reform: reducing the metropolitan examination quota, halting the sale of offices, cutting redundant posts, keeping capital officials from promotion outside their ministries, assigning clerks by specialty, discarding obsolete precedents, breaking the entrenched habits of banner troops, forbidding scholars and officials to use opium, establishing separate civil-service subjects in mathematics and technical arts, abolishing the military examination, changing drill methods, sending sons of meritorious families to study abroad, and fostering industry and craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 尤原皇上鑑天災之屢警，念民困之莫蘇，懍內政之宜修，知外患之難弭，毋始勤終怠，毋狃目前而忘遠慮。」

translations.literal: Above all I pray the Emperor will take warning from repeated natural disasters, think of the people's distress that cannot be relieved, keep in mind that internal government must be repaired, know that external peril is hard to quell, never begin diligently and end in slackness, and never cling to the present while forgetting far-sighted concern.
translations.idiomatic: Above all I pray that Your Majesty will heed the repeated warnings of natural disasters, remember the people's distress that cannot be eased, feel that internal government must be repaired, know that external peril is hard to remove, never start with zeal and finish in slackness, and never fix on the present while forgetting long-range plans."

sentences.zh: 時中外諸臣條奏，多言變法袪積習。

translations.literal: At the time memorials from court and country mostly spoke of reform and removing accumulated habits.
translations.idiomatic: At the time memorials from officials at court and in the provinces mostly spoke of reform and uprooting entrenched habits.

sentences.zh: 模言：「推行宜漸，根本宜急。

translations.literal: Mo said: "Implementation should be gradual; fundamentals should be urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Mo said, "Reforms should be introduced gradually, but fundamentals must be addressed at once.

sentences.zh: 聚闒茸嗜利之輩以期富強，止於舊法外增一法，不得謂之變法；

translations.literal: To gather worthless, profit-seeking men in hope of making the country rich and strong, and merely to add one law outside the old laws, cannot be called reform;
translations.idiomatic: To gather worthless men greedy for profit in the hope of making the country rich and strong, and merely to add one new law beside the old ones, is not reform;

sentences.zh: 於積習外增一習，不得謂之袪積習。

translations.literal: to add one habit outside accumulated habits cannot be called removing accumulated habits.
translations.idiomatic: to add one new habit beside the old ones is not uprooting entrenched habits.

sentences.zh: 欲求富強，當先崇節儉，廣教化，卹農商。」

translations.literal: If one wishes strength and wealth, one should first honor frugality, spread education, and show concern for farmers and merchants."
translations.idiomatic: If one seeks strength and wealth, one should first promote frugality, extend education, and show concern for farmers and merchants."

sentences.zh: 其恉意大率類此。

translations.literal: His meaning was broadly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His views were broadly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 模督陝甘數年，銳欲開礦制械，興學廣教，皆以用不足，不能盡舉，累疏乞罷。

translations.literal: Mo governed Shaanxi-Gansu for several years, keen to open mines, manufacture arms, and expand schools and education; all for lack of funds could not be fully carried out, and he repeatedly memorialized asking to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Mo governed Shaanxi-Gansu for several years and was eager to open mines, manufacture arms, and expand schools and education, but for lack of funds could carry out none of these fully. He repeatedly memorialized asking to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，述職入覲，道疾，留陝西。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he went to court to report on his duties, fell ill on the road, and remained in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he went to court to report on his duties, fell ill on the journey, and remained in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 俄調補兩廣總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西幸，迎謁蒲州，再乞休，不允，乃力疾上官。

translations.literal: When the two empresses went west on tour, he welcomed them at Puzhou, again begged to retire, was not permitted, and took up his post while ill.
translations.idiomatic: When the two empresses fled west, he welcomed them at Puzhou, again begged to retire, was refused, and took up his post despite illness.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，疏請裁減宦官，略言：「宦官干政，史不絕書，我朝家法嚴明，從未有內監預聞政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he memorialized asking to cut eunuchs, stating in brief: "Eunuchs meddling in government fill history without cease; our dynasty's household law is strict and bright, and never before have palace eunuchs been privy to state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he memorialized asking to reduce the number of eunuchs, stating in brief, "Eunuchs interfering in government appear throughout history without interruption. Our dynasty's household law is strict and clear, and never before have palace eunuchs been allowed to hear state affairs.

sentences.zh: 然除弊如除莠，留其芽蘗，終恐發生，宜大加裁汰。

translations.literal: Yet eliminating abuses is like eliminating weeds: leave the sprouts and shoots and in the end they will surely grow again; a great cut should be made.
translations.idiomatic: Yet eliminating abuses is like weeding: leave the sprouts and shoots and they will grow again in the end. A thorough reduction is needed.

sentences.zh: 內廷差使悉可改用士人，定宮府一體之制，永不再選內監，非唯一時盛事，實亦千古美談。」

translations.literal: Palace errands could all be assigned to scholars; fix a system of unity between palace and government, never again select eunuchs—not only a glorious affair of the moment but also a noble tale for all ages."
translations.idiomatic: Palace errands could all be assigned to scholars. Establish a system in which palace and government are one, and never again select eunuchs. This would be not only a glorious achievement of the moment but a noble example for all ages."

sentences.zh: 別疏言：「變通政治，宜務本原。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he said: "In reforming government, one should attend to fundamentals.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he said, "In reforming government one must attend to fundamentals.

sentences.zh: 本原在朝廷，必朝廷實能愛國愛民，乃能以愛國愛民責百官；

translations.literal: The fundamental lies in the court; only if the court truly can love the country and love the people can it demand love of country and people from the hundred officials;
translations.idiomatic: The fundamental lies in the court. Only if the court truly loves the country and loves the people can it require love of country and people from all officials;

sentences.zh: 必朝廷先無自私自利，乃能以不自私不自利望天下。

translations.literal: only if the court first has no selfishness or self-interest can it expect the world to be unselfish and unself-seeking.
translations.idiomatic: only if the court is first free of selfishness and private gain can it expect the world to be free of selfishness and private gain.

sentences.zh: 轉移之道，一曰除壅蔽，一曰去畛域，一曰務遠大。

translations.literal: The ways of transformation are three: remove obstruction, remove boundaries, and attend to the far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The paths of change are three: remove obstruction, remove narrow divisions, and pursue what is far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 朝廷當以身作則，克己勝私，否則雖日言變通，無由獲變通之效。」

translations.literal: The court should take the lead in example, overcome the self and triumph over selfishness; otherwise though one speaks of reform daily, there is no way to obtain the effect of reform."
translations.idiomatic: The court must set the example, restrain itself and overcome selfishness. Otherwise, though one speaks of reform every day, there is no way to achieve its effects."

sentences.zh: 粵故多盜，模定清鄉章程，信賞必罰。

translations.literal: Guangdong had long had many bandits; Mo fixed regulations for rural pacification, rewarding faith and punishing sure.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had long been infested with bandits. Mo established regulations for rural pacification, with sure rewards and sure punishments.

sentences.zh: 凡練軍分屯，許所在州縣節制。

translations.literal: All drilled troops were distributed in garrisons and allowed to be directed by the prefectures and counties where they were posted.
translations.idiomatic: Drilled troops were posted in garrisons and placed under the control of the prefectures and counties where they were stationed.

sentences.zh: 一歲中捕斬名盜千餘人，欽、廉、肇、羅諸屬盜藪，皆次第削平。

translations.literal: In one year more than a thousand notorious bandits were captured and executed; the bandit lairs of Qinzhou, Lianzhou, Zhaoqing, Luoding, and other subordinates were all reduced in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Within one year more than a thousand notorious bandits were captured and executed, and the bandit strongholds of Qinzhou, Lianzhou, Zhaoqing, Luoding, and other districts were successively wiped out.

sentences.zh: 模謂民貧思亂，非殺可止，令府縣設勸工廠，囚不至死者令入廠教養。

translations.literal: Mo said that when the people are poor they think of rebellion—not something stopping by killing alone; he ordered prefectures and counties to establish workhouses and had prisoners not liable to death enter the factories for instruction and support.
translations.idiomatic: Mo said that poverty drives people toward rebellion and that killing alone cannot stop it. He ordered prefectures and counties to establish workhouses and had prisoners not sentenced to death enter them for training and support.

sentences.zh: 廣東名饒富，然取諸民者已重於他行省，歲不足五百餘萬，則取之賭規，仍不足，則貸之外人。

translations.literal: Guangdong was famed as rich, yet what was taken from the people already weighed heavier than in other provinces; when yearly revenue fell short of more than five million, they took from gambling fees; still short, they borrowed from outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong was famed for its wealth, yet levies on the people already exceeded those of other provinces. When annual revenue fell more than five million taels short, the deficit was made up from gambling fees; when that was still insufficient, money was borrowed from outsiders.

sentences.zh: 模睹民力已屈，追呼不得寬，欲有所興革，皆坐中沮。

translations.literal: Mo saw the people's strength already bent, tax collection could not be eased, and whenever he wished to institute reforms he was blocked midway.
translations.idiomatic: Mo saw that the people were already exhausted, that tax collection could not be relaxed, and that every reform he proposed was blocked in mid-course.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請疾，甫受代，九月，卒於廣州，贈太子少保，諡勤肅。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized pleading illness; just after his successor arrived, in the ninth month he died at Guangzhou; posthumously promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous name Qinsu.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized pleading illness. Just after his successor arrived, he died at Guangzhou in the ninth month. He was posthumously promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Qinsu.

sentences.zh: 模自為諸生，食貧力學，與平湖優貢生顧廣譽、震澤諸生陳壽熊、吳江舉人沈曰富以道義相勗。

translations.literal: From his days as a licentiate Mo was poor and studied hard; with Gu Guangyu, senior licentiate of Pinghu, Chen Shouxiong, licentiate of Zhenze, and Shen Yuefu, juren of Wujiang, he encouraged one another in principle and duty.
translations.idiomatic: From his days as a licentiate Mo lived in poverty and studied hard. With Gu Guangyu, senior licentiate of Pinghu, Chen Shouxiong, licentiate of Zhenze, and Shen Yuefu, juren of Wujiang, he encouraged one another in principle and duty.

sentences.zh: 既通籍，大學士閻敬銘、總督楊昌濬皆嘗論薦，不以告模，模亦不謝也。

translations.literal: After he entered the roster of officials, Grand Secretary Yan Jingming and Governor-General Yang Changjun both at times spoke in recommendation of him without telling Mo, and Mo did not thank them either.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered official service, Grand Secretary Yan Jingming and Governor-General Yang Changjun both recommended him at times without telling him, and Mo never thanked them for it.

sentences.zh: 儉約自將，不立崖岸，恂恂卑下，將吏爭為用，而無敢以私幹者。

translations.literal: Frugal and self-restrained, he set up no lofty barrier; modest and deferential, officers and clerks vied to serve him and none dared approach him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and self-disciplined, he put on no air of superiority. Gentle and unassuming, his officers and clerks competed to serve him, yet none dared approach him with private requests.

sentences.zh: 卒後，蘭州、迪化皆允建專祠。

translations.literal: After his death, Lanzhou and Dihua were both permitted to build dedicated shrines.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, permission was granted to build dedicated shrines to him at Lanzhou and Dihua.

sentences.zh: 李興銳，字勉林，湖南瀏陽人。

translations.literal: Li Xingrui, style Minlin, native of Liuyang, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingrui, courtesy name Minlin, was a native of Liuyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 粵寇亂，以諸生治鄉團。

translations.literal: During the Taiping rebellion in Guangdong he organized local militia as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping rebellion in Guangdong he organized local militia while still a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓治軍東下，檄主軍糈，駐祁門。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan marched east with his army, he was ordered by dispatch to manage army provisions and stationed at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan marched east with his army, Xingrui was ordered by dispatch to manage army provisions and was stationed at Qimen.

sentences.zh: 江南饑民就食者萬計，興銳慮為寇乘，先期結筏以濟，獲安全，敘知縣。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of starving people from Jiangnan came for food; Xingrui feared the bandits would take advantage, so beforehand he built rafts to ferry them across and kept them safe; he was rewarded with appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of starving people from Jiangnan came seeking food. Xingrui feared the rebels would exploit the situation, so he built rafts in advance to ferry them across and kept them safe. He was rewarded with appointment as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 數薦知府。

translations.literal: Repeatedly recommended for prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly recommended for appointment as prefect.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，唐義訓、金國琛兩軍頓徽州，索餉譁變。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, the armies of Tang Yixun and Jin Guochen encamped at Huizhou and mutinied over unpaid rations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongzhi the armies of Tang Yixun and Jin Guochen were encamped at Huizhou and mutinied over unpaid rations.

sentences.zh: 興銳聞之，單騎叩其壁，諭之曰：「若輩不遠千里，從軍討賊，為富貴計耳，奈何自戕為？

translations.literal: Xingrui heard of it, rode alone to their camp, and addressed them: "You came a thousand li to follow the army against bandits for the sake of wealth and rank—why harm yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Xingrui heard of it, rode alone to their camp, and addressed them: "You came a thousand li to join the army against the rebels for wealth and rank—why turn on yourselves?

sentences.zh: 使寇知之而躡吾後，吾無焦類矣！

translations.literal: If the bandits learn of it and follow at our heels, not one of us will be left alive!
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels learn of this and follow at our heels, not one of us will survive!

sentences.zh: 餉不給，咎在台。

translations.literal: If rations are not supplied, the fault lies with the commissariat.
translations.idiomatic: If rations are not supplied, the fault lies with the commissariat.

sentences.zh: 期以三日，逾期請殺我！」

translations.literal: I give you three days; if the deadline passes, ask to kill me!
translations.idiomatic: I give you three days. If the deadline passes, you may ask to kill me!"

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「唯命！」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "We obey!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers answered, "We obey!"

sentences.zh: 乃潛訪主謀者三人，白國籓僇之，事定。

translations.literal: Then he secretly identified the three ringleaders, reported them to Guofan, who executed them, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly identified the three ringleaders, reported them to Guofan, who had them executed, and the affair was settled.

sentences.zh: 金陵既克，儲平餘銀四十餘萬。

translations.literal: After Jinling was taken, the treasury held a surplus of more than four hundred thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinling was captured, the treasury held a surplus of more than four hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 目擊戎燼後殭屍蔽野，因出所餘購義塚一區，聚暴骨瘞之。

translations.literal: Seeing corpses covering the fields after the fires of war, he spent the surplus to buy a public graveyard and gathered exposed bones to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing corpses covering the fields after the fires of war, he used the surplus to purchase a public burial ground and gathered exposed bones for interment.

sentences.zh: 八年，調直隸，補大名府，洊昇道員，乞終養。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Zhili, appointed to Daming Prefecture, repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant, and begged to retire to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Zhili, appointed prefect of Daming, repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant, and begged leave to retire and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 國籓再督兩江，檄綜營務，與彭玉麟規訂水師營製。

translations.literal: When Guofan again governed the Two Jiang, he was ordered by dispatch to manage camp affairs and, with Peng Yulin, drafted regulations for the navy.
translations.idiomatic: When Guofan again governed the Two Jiang, Xingrui was ordered by dispatch to manage camp affairs and, with Peng Yulin, drafted regulations for the navy.

sentences.zh: 國籓卒，李宗羲代督，亦頗信仗之。

translations.literal: After Guofan died, Li Zongxi succeeded as governor and also relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: After Guofan died, Li Zongxi succeeded him as governor and also relied heavily on Xingrui.

sentences.zh: 時日本窺台灣，江海戒嚴。

translations.literal: At the time Japan was casting covetous eyes on Taiwan and the rivers and sea were on alert.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Japan was casting covetous eyes on Taiwan, and the rivers and coast were placed on alert.

sentences.zh: 興銳言於宗羲，躬履江陰、狼山、吳淞、崇明，擇險設守，始倡緣海築砲台議。

translations.literal: Xingrui spoke to Zongxi; he personally inspected Jiangyin, Langshan, Wusong, and Chongming, chose defensible points to establish garrisons, and first advocated building coastal batteries.
translations.idiomatic: Xingrui spoke to Zongxi, personally inspected Jiangyin, Langshan, Wusong, and Chongming, chose defensible points for garrisons, and first proposed building coastal fortifications.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，綜辦上海機器製造局，博採西國新器，增建鐵船砲廠，鳩工庀材，閱十稔，規模略備。

translations.literal: At the change to the Guangxu reign he took charge of the Shanghai Machinery Bureau, widely gathered new machines from Western countries, expanded iron ship and cannon factories, gathered craftsmen and prepared materials; after ten years the scale was roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign he took charge of the Shanghai Machinery Bureau, gathered new machines from Western countries, expanded the iron ship and cannon works, assembled craftsmen, and prepared materials. After ten years the establishment was largely complete.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪去官，服竟，命偕鴻臚寺卿鄧承修往勘中越邊界。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death; when mourning ended he was ordered to accompany Grand Secretary of State Deng Chengxiu to survey the Sino-Vietnamese border.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon his mother's death. When mourning ended he was ordered to accompany Grand Secretary of State Deng Chengxiu to survey the Sino-Vietnamese border.

sentences.zh: 十二年，充出使日本大臣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he served as minister dispatched to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he served as envoy to Japan.

sentences.zh: 會遘疾，未上。

translations.literal: He happened to fall ill and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 居三年，補天津道，旋調山東東海關道。

translations.literal: After three years at home he was appointed to the Tianjin circuit and soon transferred to the Donghai Customs circuit of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was appointed Tianjin circuit intendant and soon transferred to the Donghai Customs post in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 威海為日人所據，居民惶恐，興銳建議勘地分界，主客互守，閭市獲安堵。

translations.literal: Weihai was occupied by the Japanese and the inhabitants were terrified; Xingrui proposed surveying the land and fixing boundaries so hosts and guests would each keep their areas, and the market towns regained peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese held Weihai, the people were terrified. Xingrui proposed surveying boundaries so Chinese and Japanese could each keep their zones, and the towns returned to normal life.

sentences.zh: 其辦交涉，獨條理精整，事可許者，一諾輒立辦；

translations.literal: In handling foreign affairs he alone was precise and orderly; when a matter could be granted, one promise and it was promptly done;
translations.idiomatic: In diplomacy he alone was precise and orderly. When something could be agreed, his word meant immediate action;

sentences.zh: 遇所不可，則抗辯廣坐，常服遠人。

translations.literal: when it could not be done, he argued in open assembly and often won over the foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: when it could not, he argued before the full assembly and often won over the foreigners.

sentences.zh: 遷長蘆鹽運使，歷福建按察使、布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Changlu salt commissioner and served successively as provincial judge and provincial treasurer of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He became Changlu salt commissioner and later served as provincial judge and treasurer of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢撫江西。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 拳匪釁作，頑民相率不靖，旬日間毀教堂數十，掠教民財產，積案二千餘。

translations.literal: When the Boxer trouble broke out, unruly people rose in succession; within ten days dozens of churches were destroyed and missionaries' property plundered, with more than two thousand cases accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer rising broke out, lawless elements followed suit. Within ten days dozens of churches were wrecked and missionaries' property looted, leaving more than two thousand cases on the books.

sentences.zh: 興銳劾罷疏防官十餘人，限三月定讞，議償卹費八十餘萬，唯節餉以彌罅漏。

translations.literal: Xingrui impeached and removed more than ten negligent officials, set a three-month limit to settle verdicts, proposed compensation and condolence payments of more than eight hundred thousand taels, and relied only on economizing military pay to fill the gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Xingrui impeached more than ten negligent officials, set a three-month deadline for verdicts, and proposed more than eight hundred thousand taels in compensation—all to be covered by cutting military expenses.

sentences.zh: 和議成，償款累百萬，仍以節餉資挹注；

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, indemnities totaled millions, and he still drew on economized military funds to cover them;
translations.idiomatic: After peace was signed, indemnities ran into the millions, and he still covered them by cutting military spending;

sentences.zh: 猶不足，則取之土藥釐榷，絕不累民間毫末。

translations.literal: when that was still insufficient, he took it from levies on native opium, never burdening the people in the least.
translations.idiomatic: when that was still not enough, he drew on opium excise revenue and never laid the burden on ordinary people.

sentences.zh: 署南贛鎮申道發統軍驕蹇不奉法，首劾罷之，軍紀始肅。

translations.literal: Acting Nangan commander Shen Daofa commanded his army with arrogance and disobedience to the law; Xingrui was the first to impeach and remove him, and only then did military discipline become strict.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Nangan commander Shen Daofa led a proud, lawless army. Xingrui impeached him first, and only then did discipline tighten.

sentences.zh: 興銳事國籓久，論治壹循軌跡，重實行。

translations.literal: Xingrui had long served Guofan; in discussing governance he followed one track throughout and stressed practical execution.
translations.idiomatic: Having long served under Guofan, Xingrui governed by a single consistent method and valued practical results.

sentences.zh: 是時上方鄉新政，乃以十事上，曰：開特科，整學校，課官吏，設銀行，鑄銀幣，維圜法，立保險，修農政，講武備，而歸本於用人，為安內攘外之策，言至深切。

translations.literal: At that time the court was turning toward new policies; he therefore submitted ten proposals: open special examinations, reform schools, assess officials, establish banks, mint silver coins, maintain currency standards, set up insurance, improve agricultural administration, strengthen military preparedness—and return to the root in the selection of men—as a policy to pacify within and resist without; his words were deeply earnest.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then turning toward reform. He submitted ten proposals: special examinations, school reform, official assessment, banks, silver coinage, currency standards, insurance, agricultural policy, and military preparedness—all rooted in appointing the right men as the strategy for internal order and external defense. His memorial was deeply earnest.

sentences.zh: 旋移撫廣東。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to govern Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to govern Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，署閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he acted as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he served as acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 閩自軍興，局所林立，有善後、濟用、勸捐、稽覈、稅釐諸目，叢弊益甚。

translations.literal: Since military troubles began in Fujian, bureaus had sprung up everywhere—postwar relief, emergency funds, donation drives, auditing, tax collection, and the like—and abuses grew ever thicker.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, Fujian had sprouted bureaus for relief, emergency funds, donations, auditing, and tax collection, and abuses multiplied.

sentences.zh: 興銳受事，裁諸局所，並為財政局，事權始一。

translations.literal: When Xingrui took office he abolished the various bureaus and merged them into a finance bureau, and authority was unified for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Xingrui abolished the bureaus and merged them into a single finance office, unifying authority at last.

sentences.zh: 於是釐定常備軍制，汰虛冗，節浮費，而閩事稍稍振矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fixed regulations for the standing army, eliminated empty posts and waste, cut extravagant expenses, and Fujian affairs gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: He then standardized the standing army, cut dead weight and waste, and Fujian affairs slowly revived.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，調署兩江。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to act in the two Jiang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to act as governor-general of Jiangsu and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 旋病卒，諡勤恪。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died of illness and was given the posthumous title Qinke.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness and received the posthumous title Qinke.

sentences.zh: 史念祖，字繩之，江蘇江都人，刑部尚書致儼孫。

translations.literal: Shi Nianzu, courtesy name Shengzi, was a native of Jiangdu in Jiangsu and grandson of Minister of Justice Zhi Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Nianzu, styled Shengzi, came from Jiangdu in Jiangsu and was the grandson of Minister of Justice Zhi Yan.

sentences.zh: 念祖幼穎異，好讀兵家言。

translations.literal: Nianzu was precocious as a child and loved to read military texts.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Nianzu was exceptionally bright and loved reading military classics.

sentences.zh: 逾冠，入貲為通判。

translations.literal: After coming of age he purchased office as a subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: After coming of age he bought office as a subprefect.

sentences.zh: 從喬松年軍解蒙城圍，有功。

translations.literal: Following Qiao Songnian's army he relieved the siege of Mengcheng and won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Qiao Songnian, he helped lift the siege of Mengcheng and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁戰歿曹州，捻益熾，皖北麋沸。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen died in battle at Caozhou; the Nian grew fiercer and northern Anhui seethed.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengge Rinchen fell at Caozhou, the Nian grew stronger and northern Anhui boiled with unrest.

sentences.zh: 念祖率師复英山，克高圩。

translations.literal: Nianzu led troops to recover Yingshan and took Gaowei.
translations.idiomatic: Nianzu led troops to recover Yingshan and took Gaowei.

sentences.zh: 雉河集者，張洛行老巢也，英翰守之，陷重圍，誓必死，念祖計出之，而自駐其地，期以二十日相見城下。

translations.literal: Zhiheji was Zhang Luoxing's old stronghold; Yinghan defended it, fell into a tight siege, and vowed to die; Nianzu devised a plan to get him out and himself took station there, agreeing to meet below the walls in twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiheji was Zhang Luoxing's old headquarters. Yinghan held it under siege and swore to die there. Nianzu devised a plan to extract him, then took the post himself and promised to meet Yinghan below the walls in twenty days.

sentences.zh: 乃為均糧法，數卻寇。

translations.literal: He then instituted an equalized grain-tax method and several times repulsed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted an equalized grain levy and beat back the rebels several times.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐堞上彈琵琶，教士卒歌，寇出視，皆驚嘆。

translations.literal: He once sat on the parapet playing the pipa and teaching the soldiers songs; the bandits came out to look and were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Once he sat on the battlements playing the pipa and teaching his men songs. The rebels came to watch and were astonished.

sentences.zh: 一日，聞槍砲聲，知援至，與寇戰，乃令居民登陴守，別選銳卒四千分道夾擊，縱橫掃蕩，寇大潰，謁英翰止逾二日雲。

translations.literal: One day, hearing gunfire, he knew relief had arrived; fighting the bandits, he ordered the inhabitants to man the walls while he chose four thousand elite troops to strike from separate routes in a pincer, sweeping all before him; the bandits were utterly routed; he met Yinghan only a little over two days later, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: One day he heard gunfire and knew relief had come. He put the townspeople on the walls, chose four thousand elite troops for a pincer attack, and routed the rebels completely. He met Yinghan just over two days later, the story goes.

sentences.zh: 數保道員。

translations.literal: He was several times recommended for circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly recommended for promotion to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 論曰：寇亂初平，安民保土，自以吏治為先，然非負文武幹用如寶楨諸人，亦不易言效也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When the rebellions were first pacified, settling the people and securing the land naturally put civil administration first; yet without men of combined civil and military capacity like Baozhen and the others, it was not easy to speak of results.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When the rebellions were first suppressed, restoring order naturally meant putting civil administration first. Yet without men of both civil and military talent like Baozhen and his peers, such results were hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 寶楨政尚威猛，瀚章治參清靜，而昌濬則不免於姑息。

translations.literal: Baozhen's government favored stern force; Hanzhang's administration was rather quiet and restrained; Changjun could not avoid indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen governed with stern force, Hanzhang with quiet restraint, and Changjun could not escape the charge of leniency.

sentences.zh: 樹聲有智略，秉璋稱綜覈。

translations.literal: Shusheng had strategic talent; Bingzhang was praised for comprehensive scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng was resourceful in strategy; Bingzhang was known for thorough, exacting administration.

sentences.zh: 榮光、士傑皆善於用兵，而疏於行政。

translations.literal: Rongguang and Shijie were both skilled in using troops but remiss in civil administration.
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang and Shijie were both skilled commanders but weaker as administrators.

sentences.zh: 興銳重實效，念祖好行權。

translations.literal: Xingrui stressed practical results; Nianzu liked to exercise expedients.
translations.idiomatic: Xingrui valued practical results; Nianzu favored bold expedients.

sentences.zh: 模獨識議宏遠，能見本原。

translations.literal: Mo alone had far-reaching vision in policy and could see to the root.
translations.idiomatic: Mo alone had far-reaching vision and could see to the root of affairs.

sentences.zh: 此十人中雖治績不必盡同，其賢者至今猶絓人口，庶幾不失曾、左之遺風歟。

translations.literal: Among these ten men, although their governing achievements were not all the same, the worthy among them are still on people's lips today—perhaps they did not fall short of the legacy of Zeng and Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: These ten men did not govern alike, yet the best are still remembered today—perhaps they did not fall far from the tradition of Zeng Guofan and Zuo Zongtang.
